The Word Itself Is God

_Teneyam vaangmayi murtih pratyaksha vartate hareh |
Sevacchravanat pathat darshanat papanashini ||
Tavat sansarachakre'smin bhramate agyanatah puman |
Yavat karnagatam nasti Adhyaru-kirtan-kshanam ||_
(This — his speech — stands here manifest as the very verbal form of Hari; by serving it, hearing it, reciting it, and beholding it, all sin is destroyed. So long as even a moment of Adhyaru's kirtan has not entered a person's ears, he keeps wandering, out of ignorance, in this wheel of worldly existence.)

The Word is God. Accordingly, Adhyaruji's speech is the verbal embodiment of the Supreme Lord of all. Therefore, by hearing, reflecting on, and deeply contemplating Adhyaruji's words, by reciting them, by beholding them, and by serving them, all sins are destroyed — for this is truly the verbal embodiment of Shri Hari himself.

Ramkabir
A Few Words (From the First Edition)

By remembrance of God's name and by worship of one's mother and father, Ganapati is worshipped first among all the gods. Adhyaruji first composed a ras (devotional song) for Ganapati, but forgot to offer salutation to Ram and Krishna, the Lords of all; so he wrote an abhog (a closing verse naming its own author) about this failing of his. Because of this his composition would not proceed further; so he made a plea (to God), after which the 27 padas came to be composed.

These padas possess every quality of true poetry, and each pada is like a mantra. Because the desire (vasana) of a desire-bound soul is released through them, Jivanji selected 28 padas and commanded his disciples to make a collection of Adhyaruji's padas.

Wise disciples compiled them and kept them as part of their daily recitation. Lazy and negligent disciples lost them through carelessness. Whoever compiled Adhyaruji's padas and put them to use can be freed even from the ghost-realm of a desire-bound spirit.

Jagdishbhai has had this booklet (gutko) printed and has thereby poured grace upon simple devotees (uda bhakts). These few words are for that booklet, and my blessings go with it. Let the simple devotee become alert on reading this much. Adhyaruji sings:

_Dekhadyo re dekhadyo re Shri Guru-e bhandar, Parbrahm samaran rupiyo_
(The Guru has revealed, has revealed, the treasure — in the form of the remembrance of Parbrahm, the Supreme Being.)

With this treasure in the form of remembrance (samaran) available, the devotee ought not to be sorrowful, because the treasure is truly his own. Now, after this word of caution, I shall rest — for I have written these few words from my sickbed, at Jagdish's insistence; so make good use of them. Keep the promises made in this booklet and by Jivanji. Compile the 28 padas. This is my Ramkabir. To every simple devotee, my Ramkabir.

Acknowledgement: In publishing this booklet, Bhakt Hargovindbhai Ramdas (of Siyabag) gave much help, and Pandit Shri Motidasji too gave much cooperation, for which I offer them my thanks.

_Patan Padmo avataro, je Gokulno Kaan |
Sukh sagar sada Jivana, je diyo Sudama daan ||1||_
(1. In Patan, Padmo took incarnation — he who is the Kaan [Krishna] of Gokul. O Jivana, ever an ocean of bliss, he who gave his gift of grace to Sudama.)

Yadunath's Ramkabir.

Ramkabir, The Kirtan's Peacock-Call

_Kujantam Padmanabh Parbrahmeti madhuram madhurakshram |
Aaruhya kavita shakham vande Dhanraj kokilam ||_
(I bow to Dhanraj, the cuckoo who, perched on the branch of poetry, sweetly calls out the sweet syllables "Padmanabh, Parbrahm.")

Just as Valmiki, like a cuckoo perched on the branches of poetry, sang the multitude of Ramchandra's virtues, so too Dhanraj Adhyaruji, like a cuckoo, has cooed out the praise of the virtues of Lord Padmanabh; and the notes of that cooing still today moisten the hearts of loving and wise devotees alike.

To this, Jivanji Maharaj bears witness. Before beholding, through Dhanraj's eyes of knowledge, the vision of Lord Padmanabh's virtuous form, let us first behold what Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj has said regarding Padmanabh's incarnation.

_Jug sarapo jogade, Gurjar khand gumar |
Shap utaro Jivana, lino Padmanabh avatar ||1||_
(1. The age had wearied and cursed the foolish land of Gujarat. O Jivana, to lift that curse, the incarnation of Padmanabh was taken.)

In the age of Kali, the naivety of a bewildered Gujarat had begun to be exploited — by the violence of the Shakta sect, by the Kapalik and Bhairava rites of the Shaiva sect, by the immorality of the Vama-marg (left-hand path), or by the karma-and-dharma-bound cravings of non-Jain philosophies. This was a curse upon Gujarat, and it was precisely to remove this curse that the incarnation of Lord Padmanabh took place.

At Daksha's sacrifice, Prajapati (Daksha) had incurred a curse of ritual barrenness because of his enmity toward Shiva. To remove this, the Lord had given his own word: "O Prajapati, in the age of Kali I shall take incarnation in your lineage and deliver your lineage from that barren state." This was accomplished through the incarnation of Padmanabh.

Patan and Siddhpatan have been the field of action of Lord Kapil, founder of the Sankhya philosophy — he who repaid the debt owed to the mother who bore him by giving mother Devahuti knowledge of the eternal, and who freed her from attachment to the perishable body. Because of this, this sacred land on the bank of the Saraswati has earned the title "Dharmaranya," the forest of dharma. Here the culture of knowledge, devotion, and detachment has had the fortune to flourish.

This is also the very place of the sacred guru-disciple pair, Lord Dattatreya and Yadu, who together brought knowledge, devotion, and detachment into one. The words of Yadu's own experience — Yadu, who had suffered from his father's curse — on beholding Lord Dattatreya still resound today: "Who are you? At the sight of you all my afflictions dissolve; the threefold torments are stilled." Even today, such darshan is needed to cross over worldly existence. Every traveler on the path of liberation, and Dhanraj Adhyaruji too, experiences this very state through the darshan of Lord Padmanabh.

_Devne ghenghat hoy re swami, Shri Padmanabh pasayo kari |
Padmanabh pasayo karine, jamna te jokham gaya tali ||1||_
(1. O Lord, even the gods know [unclear] — Shri Padmanabh has shown grace; by Padmanabh's grace, the peril of Yama has been turned aside.)

Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj has said that Padmo, who manifested in Patan, is the very Kahan (Krishna) of Gokul; Dhanraj himself affirms this, as follows, at the close of a kadavu.

_Avatariya chhe re avatariya chhe re,
Gokulna Kahan Shri Padmanabh Purushottam ||2||_
(2. He has taken incarnation, he has taken incarnation — the Kahan of Gokul is Shri Padmanabh, the Supreme Person.)

Saints and devotees compare the essence of Krishna, manifested in the land of Vraj, to a mango tree. The devotee-poet Narsinh Mehta too says, "The mango tree of blessed Gokul has blossomed…" In the very same way it is said of Padmanabh, who manifested in the Dharmaranya of Patan.

_Patan aambo moriyo, jhinchyo Jhalavad |
Fal lagya chhe Malve, vedchyo chhe Gujarat ||1||_
(1. In Patan the mango tree has blossomed, Jhalavad has fenced it round; fruit has formed in Malwa, Gujarat has harvested it.)

Like Krishna, Padmanabhji too is in the form of a mango tree. The mango tree grows in fertile soil; when the season's time arrives, it blossoms. The cuckoo is drawn by the flower-clusters of the mango's blossom, just as poets are drawn by the virtuous character of the Lord. A blossoming mango tree must be fenced round with thorns for its protection; Jhalavad is such a fence. Jivanji Maharaj first made disciples in Marwad and thus set the fruit, and in Gujarat he harvested and gave out those fruits.

Dhanraj identifies this fruit as follows —

_Tilak tulsi naam ayudh, odharya Shrinath |
Samrit bole sambhalo, aapiya Vaishnav haath ||2||_
(2. Tilak, tulsi, and the Name are the weapons by which Shrinath has redeemed souls; hear what the scriptures declare — these have been placed in the hands of the Vaishnav.)

Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj says thus —

_Ramavatare vruksh nipno, Krishnavatare safal falo |
So fal Julahe chakhiyo, taanha naam boond Jivan jado ||3||_
(3. In the Ram incarnation the tree sprouted, in the Krishna incarnation it bore fruit; that fruit was tasted by the Weaver [Kabir], and there, in the drop of the divine Name, Jivan was found.)

Thus the final stage of ripening of that drop of the Name fell to Jivanji's own lot. The fruit — the divine Name — of the mango tree that is Lord Padmanabh was received by Jivanji; that same Lord Padmanabh is here today. Tilak, tulsi, the Name of Ram, and the company of saints — these four treasures — he gathered as the essence of it all. — (from the Samagam)

Ram, Krishna, Kabir, Padmanabh, and Jivanji are glimpses of the form of this one and the same Parbrahm, who has manifested at different times for the sake of fulfilling the aspirations of devotees.

_Em nit nava tuj vesh, name sev dev Murar |
Bhakt jani nav uvekhe, te eklo sansar ||4||_
(4. Thus your forms are ever new; in each name the God Murari is served. Knowing one as a devotee, he never disregards him — it is only the world that stands apart.)

In the Narada Bhakti Sutra, the guiding word for the path of devotion in the age of Kali is given thus: "Kali kevala kirtanam" — in Kali, kirtan alone suffices. Dhanraj Adhyaruji too shows, in the following way, the path to bring that Supreme Reality under one's sway.

_Teh kem kije vash aap, jeh Brahma Shankarno baap |
Teh tani surat chhe em, jaha hu ja taha muj naam ||5||_
(5. How can one bring under his own sway him who is the father even of Brahma and Shankar? His own nature is this: wherever I myself am, there is my Name.)

_Jaha jaha re jan le naam, taha taha te maro thaam_
(Wherever a person takes my Name, there and there alone is my abode.)

Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj holds the same closeness with Kabirji as he holds with Padmanabhji. Whereas to society at large, Kabirji and Padmanabhji appear to be links separated from one another, it is Jivanji Maharaj who has joined these links together, in the following way.

_Bamb baharo Jivana, dole sare na kaaj |
Chakve das Kabirji, ke Padmanabhko raaj ||6||_
(6. O Jivana, one who stands outside the reflection merely wavers, and nothing is accomplished by it; the servant Kabirji sees clearly that it is the very kingdom of Padmanabh.)

"Bamb" means reflection. The object and its reflection are not different from one another; they are shadow and counter-shadow. The appearance of separateness seen between the two is artificial and false. To imagine such separateness between Kabirji and Padmanabh is foolishness.

Dhanraj has offered Lord Padmanabh a garland of devotional poetry, whose flowers, or beads, take the form of these kirtans; through these kirtans one reaches the far shore of Parbrahm. Let us now savor the number and form of this "kekarav" — this peacock-call of kirtans.

Why is the number of these padas twenty-eight? The four Vedas, the six Shastras, and the eighteen Puranas add up to twenty-eight; it is surmised that these twenty-eight padas too stand as their symbol and essence. But a special emphasis on the principle of desireless devotion (nishkam bhakti) as true worship, together with a strong note of opposition to artificial scripture and philosophy, is heard through every pada — this very critique is voiced within the Vedas, the Puranas, and the Shok Bhavan (a section of this work). In Sadguru Jivanji's view, the purpose behind Adhyaruji's composing of these padas appears in the line: "Kund athyavis Jivana, je janake diya chhoday" (Twenty-eight are the wells, O Jivana, which the Father has granted release from).

Having mentioned the number of kirtans, let us now savor a little of their essence. Among these twenty-eight kirtans, grouped by form, there are five Ras, three Dhol, two Bhavan, two Karaj, and four Kadva, and these draw the greatest attention; besides them, the remaining kirtans too each hold their own distinct merit.

Five Ras: Here the number of Ras is five. In the Shrimad Bhagavat too there are five, on account of which it is popularly known as the "Ras Panchadhyayi." The Lord ordained the Ras in order to shatter the pride of Kamdev, the god of desire. Through the Ras, the soul is freed from the corruption of the five sense-objects. Kamdev has five weapons; Krishnachandra, through the Ras, has blunted these weapons that are the sense-objects.

Three Dhol: Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj has called the Dhol the crown-jewel of scripture. The unfolding of the Dhol raga makes an ocean of bliss surge forth. At any wedding, the singing of a Dhol draws special attention; hearing a Dhol makes one forget bodily awareness, a state yogis call "sahaj samadhi," natural absorption. In this state attraction and aversion come to rest, and a boundless flood of bliss surges up. Dhol songs are sung only for one's own chosen deity — an auspicious occasion, the guru, the sun-god, or Ram-Krishna. Adhyaruji reaches this goal through the Vadu Dhol, the Padam Dhol, and the Prithvi Dhol. The Sant Sohago and the Dhol are bound up with one another.

Two Karaj: The soul's tasks are two — one, to be freed from the wheel of birth and death that is the bondage of karma, and the other, to attain one's chosen deity. Through the turning wheel of the Lodhi Karaj, the means of avoiding rebirth in the womb is obtained; for this, taking refuge in Hari, the Supreme Lord, is essential. The expression of the wish to take refuge in the deity one has resolved upon is given, in the Vadi Karaj, thus:

_Te Hari Parbrahm je Parbrahm Swami Padmanabhji tam sharanam_
(That Hari, the Supreme Being — O Lord Parbrahm, Padmanabhji, I take refuge in you.)

The contemplation of the individual soul and the Supreme Soul is set out in the Heli, the Saheli, and the Ghodli, while the Brahmaruli is an appeal addressed to Brahman.

Two Bhavan: In the Shok Bhavan, the means by which the movement of Time — which makes even Hari, Har, and Brahma weep — comes to find its rest is shown as follows:

_Je Harinaam sada jape, seve tulsi re sant,
Gopichandan shir vahe re, drashti na aave re kaal_
(The saint who always chants the Name of Hari, and serves the tulsi plant, and bears the sacred gopichandan mark upon his head — to him, Time itself does not even come into view.)

In the Harsh Bhavan it is shown that for eternal happiness, all the world's opinion should become one in taking refuge in the Guru, and that the Hari-mantra should be worshipped through contemplation on the nature of the Self.

Four Kadva: In the Parbrahm Padbandh Kadvu, one beholds the form of Krishna, the perfect Brahman, and the Lord's tender affection for his devotee; seeing the command Brahma gave to Dharmaraj in order to safeguard the honor of the devotee, the greatness of the Lord's devotee becomes clear. Hari is one alone, who fulfills our heart's desires; through this, devotion arises in all moving and unmoving beings, and the bondage of worldly existence is severed by devotion.

Fearlessness is the precondition for the wager that is liberation. Fearlessness in the face of Time is found only with the Lord's saints; even Brahma and Shiva do not have the right to make such a wager.

Certainty of Hari's oneness, and unshakeable faith in it, form the very basis of the Aarti. Through the turmeric-red mark of simple devotion, the truly whole man in whom it is set awakens to the nature of his own Self, and thereby attains the fruit his mind desires.

In the Khandana, worldly craving itself is shown as the cause of birth and death, and the necessity of the company of saints, for becoming a Vaishnav, is set out. The Umavalo gives a vision of the divine form. To reach the goal that is the swing of desireless devotion, the conditions of supplication laid out in the Pasavala should be sincerely and whole-heartedly accepted by the earnest devotee.

My heart is troubled that, from concern over the limits of space, this taste of the kirtans' essence may not give seekers full satisfaction. This is an attempt to fill an ocean from a small pitcher. My prayer to the Lord is only that it may extend far enough to fill whole ponds of that essence.

In this new edition of the kirtans, the changes made in some of them will draw the attention of those who recite them daily. It is a heartfelt request that everyone follow this new edition with love. In this new edition, as far as possible, comparison has been made with old manuscripts. Taking as its base the manuscript written down, in Jivanji Maharaj's own presence, by Haridas of Nadiad, very necessary corrections have been made [some further detail here is unclear in the source]; the oldest manuscript is the one from Patan. May all devotees take up the good fortune of sitting upon the swing of desireless devotion. This is the prayer: that the boundless grace of Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj, who shows the way to a society advancing along the path [unclear] toward God, may be attained by all.

_Raat divas eso jaanine anusaro_
(Knowing this, follow it day and night —)
[The remaining lines of this closing verse are garbled in the source and cannot be rendered reliably.]

May you bring about auspicious blessing.

With the respectful regards of Jagdish — Ramkabir.
Shri Dham Puniyad.

Atha Kim (Now, Then)

By the Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj Memorial Foundation, the fourth edition was first published in 2004; after that came the fifth edition. Going by the steadily increasing demand, one gets an idea of just how warmly this booklet has been embraced by the public. Today it is a joy to bring out this combined booklet, containing Adhyaruji's kirtans together with the sakhis expounded by Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj. The span of the first three editions was quite long — from 1962 to [unclear] — whereas the pace of the last four editions shows how popular Adhyaruji has become in society, and how deeply these kirtans have become woven into people's lives. Even with the pull toward other religions, one cannot fully measure how useful these padas and their recitation (parayan) are for us — for Adhyaru is our very life (Jivan). We need Adhyaruji every day; these padas can be recited at any time, morning to evening. I have noticed that in many families it is customary to complete a parayan in the evening or at night, whenever time allows. Going beyond mere tradition, Adhyaruji Maharaj gives us an extraordinary spiritual joy whose worth cannot be fixed by any measure. This priceless spiritual heritage — our elders used to use a certain expression for it, but the word "sumaran" actually means "true death," whereas one should say "samaran," because "samaran" means the remembrance of God's Name. So this is a humble appeal to earnest devotees: those who hold old copies of the booklet should correct this error when reciting.

In society, there has also been a demand for sakhis alongside Adhyaruji's kirtans. In publishing this edition, with its eleven vishrams (sections of rest), on behalf of the whole family, in gratitude for the unique cooperation of an anonymous devotee family — given on condition that their name not be disclosed — the Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj Memorial Foundation extends its heartfelt thanks [the sentence continues beyond this page].

...I extend [my thanks], and I would also like to express special thanks to Kanubhai Vrundavanbhai Bhagat (of Chalamli) for his cooperation in proofreading during the publication of this book. I offer the blessing that the boundless grace of Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj may rest upon his family.

The Sadguru Shri Jivanji Maharaj Memorial Foundation is bringing out several more new publications in the time ahead, and we are receiving immense, selfless cooperation from society for this work -- for which we, in turn, thank society here. For books and other publications, you may also reach us through our website: www.ramkabir.guru and www.ramkabir.org. Very soon, all of our literature will be made available online through the website. Some books can already be downloaded and read on the Google Play Store; our efforts to bring them to the Apple iPhone platform are under way. Through our website we aim to provide information useful to society, and for this we seek society's continued cooperation.

Your well-wisher,
Swami Premjivan Jagdishchandra
Dated: 4 April 2019
Vadodara.

Kirtan of Shri Padmanabhji, by Adhyaruji

_Devahutikun Jivana bhaye Kapil Muni avatar,
Dattatray Yaduke bhaye | Padmanabh Dhanraj ||1||_ (To Devahuti, O Jivan, was born the incarnation of sage Kapil Muni; to Yadu was born Dattatreya -- and now, in this age, he has come as Padmanabh Dhanraj.)

_Aap aapna [unclear] olkhi | Padmanabh Dhanraj,
Swami sevak mali Jivana kiyo bhaktko kaj ||2||_ (He recognized His own [devotees] [unclear] -- that same [Lord, now come] as Padmanabh Dhanraj; Master and servant came together, O Jivan, and he did the devotee's work.)

_Adhyaru Patan bhaye | Raykhanke Diwan,
Padmanabhki pritma | chhod diya sab maan ||3||_ (Adhyaru became, in Patan, the Diwan [minister] to Raykhan; but out of love for Padmanabh, he gave up all worldly honor.)

_[unclear -- source badly corrupted] | Gurjar khand [unclear],
Shap utaro Jivana lino [unclear] avatar ||4||_ ([This couplet's opening is illegible in the source scan; the surviving words indicate:] ...in the land of Gujarat... Jivan lifted the curse and took incarnation [as unclear].)

_Kaljag bahot kripa kari | Surat dhari mere shaam,
Patanma padhariya | Padmanabhji naam ||5||_ (In this Kali age he showed abundant grace, and my dark Lord took manifest form; he arrived in Patan under the name Padmanabhji.)

_Dhanya dhanya Padmanabhne | Jangalna chho rasiya,
Aagal paachal jhaad jhundne | vachma pote vasiya ||6||_ (Blessed, blessed is Padmanabh -- you delight in the forest wilds; with trees and groves all around, he himself dwelt in their midst.)

sections.title_en: The Ras (round-dance hymn) of the Great Ganapati
sections.translation:
Heading: Here begins the Ras (round-dance hymn) of the great Ganapati ||1||

1. Great Ganapati, the god of the mighty belly, the lord who removes obstacles, the brother [of Kartikeya] - at his feet I make my obeisance. Hari, Hari.

2. She holds the veena and the book in her hands; mounted on the swan she places her gift in the poet's hand; she destroys the very root of dull-wittedness. Hari, Hari.

3. Bowing my head at the feet of the goddess Sarasvati, by whose grace the gift of poetry is won - Lord, I shall sing the praises of Govind. Hari, Hari.

4. He who created all beings, moving and unmoving; who pervades water, land, earth and every world; and who kindled the blaze of delusion (moh). Hari, Hari.

5. He watches over the soul that dwells within the body; when it strays onto the wrong road, He turns it back. Serving Him puts an end to worldly bondage (sansar). Hari, Hari.

6. In an instant He fashions many universes and destroys them; the all-pervading One Himself dwells in the three worlds; and laughing, He makes sport of it all. Hari, Hari.

7. He is close at hand, yet the soul does not long for Him; drunk on its own deeds (karma) it will not worship Him; and death seizes it from within. Hari, Hari.

8. He makes the man without devotion perform deeds, and to reap those deeds He makes him take a body. But what deeds bind His servant? Hari, Hari.

9. In every pore of Him many universes are contained; Brahma and the other gods, Sanaka and the other sages, run in search - yet they do not reach His limit. Hari, Hari.

10. That Lord is contained alike in the body and in the universe; sages, gods, demons and men have not fathomed Him; He alone knows Himself. Hari, Hari.

11. Know that to serve Hari is unshakable happiness. Why fix your mind on this perishing thing? Nectar is being poured out for you - do not spill it. Hari, Hari.

12. Put away the craving for what pleases the senses; in heart, word and deed contemplate Vishnu; then you will pass beyond the net of worldly existence. Hari, Hari.

13. In the form of the Fish (Matsya) He slew Shankhasur; in his goodness He carried [his own] across the ocean of existence; He drove unrighteousness out of the worlds. Hari, Hari.

14. In the form of the Tortoise (Kurma) He bore up Mount Mandar; gods and demons alike plunged in and laboured; and the Ocean of Milk was churned. Hari, Hari.

15. At the time of dissolution, when the earth lay sunk in the waters, the primordial Boar (Varah) lifted her upon the tip of his tusk - when the destruction of the worlds was at hand. Hari, Hari.

16. Hiranyakashipu was renowned through the three worlds; in battle he defeated the hosts and Indra, lord of the gods; his undoing came through a sage's curse. Hari, Hari.

17. For the sake of his son and to fulfil his longing, in the form of Narsinh (the Man-Lion) He tore him open with His claws and slew the demon king. Hari, Hari.

18. For Indra's sake He undid the strength of Bali's sacrifice; as Vaman He made Bali dwell in the netherworld; and the worlds dwelt without fear. Hari, Hari.

19. As Parashuram He broke the lords of the kshatriyas; He requited the offence done to the great sage; and He established the brahmin folk. Hari, Hari.

20. He took birth as an avatar in the royal line of Raghu; the wish in the heart of Indra was fulfilled; and He showed His grace to the gods. Hari, Hari.

21. Dasharath was filled with supreme joy; the sorrow and grief of childlessness was taken away; four sons became the lamps of his line. Hari, Hari.

22. His is the name whose recitation the shruti (revealed scripture) prescribes, at the mere remembrance of which heaps of sin are destroyed - so the Vedas and the Puranas declare. Hari, Hari.

23. There Ramchandra grew day by day; as if in play the Lord accomplished every task; and He upheld his own dharma. Hari, Hari.

24. In his play he guarded the great sage's sacrifice; Hari removed the torment caused by the demons; and he redeemed the body of Ahalya. Hari, Hari.

25. In play he broke the bow of Tripurari (Shiva); at the sound of it the three worlds began to tremble; he broke it as easy sport. Hari, Hari.

26. In the three worlds there was unceasing festival; the bridegroom of Sita, the most beautiful in all three worlds; gods and men rejoiced in their hearts. Hari, Hari.

27. The four brothers, being married, set out; Parashuram's heart was pierced with rage; the mountains and crags shook. Hari, Hari.

28. Parashuram recognized him as the supreme Lord; when he strung the bow, conviction came; he knew him for the highest of the gods. Hari, Hari.

29. The Lord of play came to Ayodhya; the beautiful bridegroom was welcomed with showers of pearls; he was lovely to look upon as the moon. Hari, Hari.

30. Seeing the king bound by his word to the mother, he set aside the kingdom of Ayodhya and took on the garb of a forest exile. Hari, Hari.

31. With Lakshman and Sita, the eternal Lord went to the forest of Mount Chitrakut; [meanwhile] his father departed to the world of the gods. Hari, Hari.

32. Bharat was fetched from his mother's family; they offered him the robes and the coronation; [instead] he came to where Shri Ram was. Hari, Hari.

33. "Be gracious, Lord, and come back to the city; master, take up your father's kingdom" - so Bharat spoke with the deepest humility. Hari, Hari.

34. Ramchandra gave him counsel; Bharat set the sandals (paduka) upon the throne; and so he was given a rule he was not to enjoy himself. Hari, Hari.

35. The Lord moved on from Chitrakut; the master of divine play reached the southern country; and there he received the honour of many sages. Hari, Hari.

36. The jar-born sage [Agastya] gave him his instruction; Ramchandra went on to the Panchavati forest, holding joy in his heart. Hari, Hari.

37. A night-roaming demoness came, tormented with lust; Lakshman dealt with Shurpanakha and cut off her ears and nose. Hari, Hari.

38. Fourteen thousand demons were hunted down in battle; grieving at that, the city of Lanka turned hostile; and Marich carried out his deed [of the golden deer]. Hari, Hari.

39. He cut down the lord of the monkeys [Vali]; in his place he installed Sugriv; and gave him an unshakable kingdom. Hari, Hari.

40. On Mount Malyavan, Sugriv sustained them; the monkey [Hanuman] burned the city of Lanka and came back; and the army of monkeys gathered. Hari, Hari.

41. Ramchandra's host reached the ocean; there the monkey Nal built the bridge; and in a moment they crossed to the other side. Hari, Hari.

42. The night-rangers fell upon the battlefield; Ravan was slain together with his kin; the arrow severed all ten of his heads. Hari, Hari.

43. Joy could not be contained in all the worlds; Ramchandra took Sita and entered the city of Ayodhya. Hari, Hari.

44. In the form of Krishna he was born in Gokul; he held up Mount Govardhan on his hand; the gopis chose Govind [as their beloved]. Hari, Hari.

45. A crown of peacock feathers graces his head; by his own maya the Lord graces the three worlds; a garland of gunja berries adorns him. Hari, Hari.

46. Flute in hand, he sounds the horn; surrounded by the cowherds he goes along; in him the Vedas find the Parabrahman (the supreme reality). Hari, Hari.

47. Hari delights in every form and every hue; in Vrindavan he dances among the gopis; and yet he is the true brahmachari (the pure celibate). Hari, Hari.

48. Unfathomable, beyond all possibility, thus was he seen; he entered Gokul in the play of a child; he is the one upon whom Dhruv and Shuk sat in meditation. Hari, Hari.

49. The infinite one stayed eleven years [in Gokul]; then Akrur came with the summons; Govind, the twenty-sixth [beyond the twenty-five principles]. Hari, Hari.

50. The dark one is the Parabrahman, having no [mortal] body; yet for the sake of curds the charming one presses his demand; he is never in want of anything. Hari, Hari.

51. In the form of Buddha, Hari taught meditation and reflection; in the form of Kalanki he destroys the barbarians; and he takes care of his own people. Hari, Hari.

52. Set the dark-hued Hari within your heart; make your play in the name of Hari, lord of the three worlds; bathe in supreme bliss. Hari, Hari.

53. For the fruit of devotion (bhakti) to Vishnu and of liberation, Dhanraj himself composed this ras; do your work in the name of Hari. Hari, Hari.

Colophon: Thus the Ras of the great Ganapati is complete ||1||

Heading: Here begins the Vinati (supplication) ||2||

Refrain, repeated at the close of every verse: "Falling at your feet I make my plea."

1. You alone are the first and the beginningless, O my Lord - stainless and without form. From you came Hari, Har and Brahma; Lord, you are without limit. Falling at your feet I make my plea.

2. No one can reach your farther shore, Lord - Parabrahman (the supreme reality), whom nothing can contain. Make me, who am yours, like yourself; make this world free of maya (illusion).

3. You keep your own self hidden, Lord, and so the world is swept along. Sacrifice, charity, spiritual striving - even with these there is no end to the round of the womb.

4. This soul roams through the worlds, Lord, and does not know your essence. Masterless, it is beaten about among the four kinds of birth.

5. Brahma and the rest, Shiva, and every soul that puts on a body, Lord - some are great and some are small; but you, Lord, are unfathomable and mighty.

6. This soul was set apart, Lord, and through the gunas (the qualities of nature) it was broken up. Eighty-four lakh kinds of living beings came into being, and with them the universe was filled.

7. It let go of the universe that was its own, Lord, and fell into the delusion of worldly life; blindly it says "I" and "mine" - blind and foolish is this creature.

8. Merciful Lord, you are beyond all measure; what deliberating does the all-powerful need? Before you, what is mine? I have no being of my own at all.

9. He makes himself as nothing, Lord, and sets you within. Now do whatever pleases you, so that this ignorant one may be saved.

10. Tormented by hunger, thirst and the rest, Lord, he still hopes for pleasure; and for that he will get yet another body - ten months hanging head-downward [in the womb].

11. Moment by moment he is born and in a moment he dies, Lord; he falls into the hand of Time. Everywhere he calls things his own, yet none of it will go with him.

12. This soul has wasted its house, Lord; it went its own wilful way. Lacking devotion (bhakti) to you, it was struck down by Yama.

13. Lord, show your mercy in full measure; break up my many scattered thoughts. Grant me unshakable devotion to you, which is the treasury of liberation.

14. Brahma and the other gods look toward Vaikunth, Lord, and behold the infinite Vishnu - the king of the imperishable state; him the saints serve.

15. There is no end to your forms, Lord; your play fills the universe. In whatever way a devotee holds you in his mind, in that very form you take a body for him.

16. To whoever offers up his own self, Lord, you give grace in that measure; you yourself take on your own forms; you are the great king.

17. When the wicked torment the good, Lord, you hasten to their aid; you take on the form the occasion calls for and end their suffering that very moment.

18. You are Matsya, Kurma and Varah, Lord; Narsinh at one time; Vaman, Trikam, Parashuram, and the avatar in the line of Raghu.

19. You are Nar-Narayan and Krishna, Lord; and the forms of Buddha and Kalanki. When you are found, one sees your true nature, the Parabrahman.

20. Garud is your mount, Lord; the Kaustubh jewel is your necklace; the Shrivatsa mark shines upon you - such forms you have taken many a time.

21. You appeared in person before Brahma and the rest, Lord; you rest at ease upon Shesh; Lakshmi serves at your feet - such are your guises.

22. The soul exists by your support, Lord - the soul that is the twenty-fifth principle. Whoever leaves prakriti (nature, matter) behind and recites your name beholds the Parabrahman.

23. Where love for prakriti still remains, Lord, a man will perform many pious works; and for that he will again receive a body and reap his karma.

24. But he who counts prakriti a prison, Lord, and pines to dwell in you - if he holds to this to the very end, his dwelling is in the world of truth.

25. "Be gone, sinful prakriti!" - yet, Lord, she does not release him in the least; she drowns out the Master's word. He who yearns for it goes to that home.

26. Prakriti says: "Listen, O soul - what fault is mine? Many a time it was you who desired me; why are you angry now?"

27. As prakriti and purush (nature and spirit) spoke thus, Lord, the old affection between them broke; the soul went and merged in the Parabrahman, and the body dissolved into the five elements.

28. Yama exists because you have decreed it, Lord; that is the very law of the age. Without you, recitation, austerity, charity and compassion - all of these are mere karma.

29. Age by age the doctrines differ, Lord, and at the end of an age they perish. The Veda does not perish though all else perishes, through many ages and many dissolutions.

30. The Veda is Vishnu's own utterance, Lord, and its limit cannot be found. He upon whose support the universes rest - he is the true support.

31. One who is without your grace, Lord, defies the royal command; he has let his own dharma go up in smoke; and he takes teaching for no more than a passing camp [unclear].

32. The soul, which has no being of its own, makes its plea, Lord: "Save me, Father. Now I have found you, the all-powerful - grant just this one request."

Colophon: Thus the Vinati is complete ||2||

sections.title_en: Brahmaruli - hymn to the Supreme Brahman
sections.translation:
[Here begins Shri Brahmaruli ||3||. Every verse carries the refrain "ture brahmaruli", shortened to "ture" after the opening verses.]

1. Let us sing of the King, the Supreme Brahman (Parbrahm) - the one incomparable God. ||1||
2. Whom Hari (Vishnu), Har (Shiva) and Brahma repeat in prayer - whose qualities have no limit. ||2||
3. As a tiny insect cannot grasp the orb of the sun - ||3||
4. so gods and demons too do not comprehend You; You alone are the knowing one. ||4||
5. He fills the body and the whole cosmos - from Him come the many living beings. ||5||
6. Again and again all things arise from Him - and perish at the end of the age. ||6||
7. Again the soul is dragged along by its karma (the fruit of its deeds) - fallen into the wildfire of delusion. ||7||
8. It passes through the eighty-four lakh forms of birth - there is no end to the wombs it enters. ||8||
9. Grass, crops and grain are brought forth - by the meeting of the rain-cloud and the earth. ||9||
10. Yet the crop never knew the cloud [that made it] - for the crop is without consciousness. ||10||
11. By this illustration it has been shown - so how then should the soul know Him? ||11||
12. He who has found refuge in the Name abides [in Him] - and to such a one He makes Himself known. ||12||
13. Water creatures live long lives [in the water] - yet the creature does not know that secret. ||13||
14. He by whose word the ages move on - by whom this world spreads out. ||14||
15. He sends sap into every single leaf - behold the water at the root. ||15||
16. Many kinds of flowers and fruits are produced - see it, within hard wood. ||16||
17. It grazes on grass and gives milk, curds and ghee - it is You who appoint the cow to yield. ||17||
18. From a single drop the body is formed - [and in it] man and woman sport in passion. ||18||
19. The guardians of the worlds and the five great elements - You sustain them all, unbroken. ||19||
20. Countless ages come into being in this way - mighty is Your word. ||20||
21. Thus we know You as nirgun (without attributes) - there is none above You. ||21||
22. Giving purpose to what is insentient - by You every work is brought to its end. ||22||
23. We see only by the light of the sun - yet the ignorant man says, "I see." ||23||
24. Though he has eyes he has become blind - for without the sun there is only darkness. ||24||
25. By this truth all things have their being - beyond all qualities, You are pure Being. ||25||
26. He breaks and fashions crores of universes - He grants their powers to Hari, Har and Brahma. ||26||
27. As His mind conceives, so it comes to be - the whole expanse of the universe out of nothing. ||27||
28. O mighty One, what is Yours and what belongs to Your own - that reckoning You alone know. ||28||
29. We know You as beyond understanding and beyond conceiving - the soul's refuge is Your Name. ||29||
30. In my ignorance I have offended You - in mercy, grant me rest. ||30||
31. By Your own will You lift [me] up - take me, let Your Name cling to me. ||31||
32. Through simple, guileless bhakti (devotion) He was met face to face - the beginningless Supreme Brahman. ||32||
33. Without Your will none can see You - not Sanak and the other sages and yogis, not even in a dream. ||33||
34. Knowledge, radiance and supreme bliss [are his] - who serves his own Supreme Brahman. ||34||
35. The wind moves within a fragrance - [then] leaves the scent behind and keeps its own nature. ||35||
36. So Hari moves within the qualities [yet stays untouched by them] - attributeless One, I repeat Your Name. ||36||

[Thus ends Shri Brahmaruli, complete ||3||]

[Here begins Shri Heli ||4||. Every verse opens with the refrain "heli re" - "O friend".]

1. O friend, the Supreme Brahman who is unmanifest - He is the first, the Supreme Self. ||1||
2. O friend, He whose three portions create, sustain and dissolve. ||2||
3. O friend, Brahma and the rest are [only] souls - He does not fall within their perception. ||3||
4. O friend, the primal One, alone and unstained - yet He spreads Himself out into very many [forms]. ||4||
5. O friend, He is unmoving and imperishable - in play He makes what exists cease to exist. ||5||
6. O friend, gods, men and nagas (serpent beings) serve Him - all abide in Your dwelling. ||6||
7. O friend, Sanak and the other sages and yogis - however they search, they never reach His limit. ||7||
8. O friend, He from whom all comes into separate being - and in whom again all sets [like the sun]. ||8||
9. O friend, incomprehensible, unseen, undivided - the Vedas praise Him without ceasing. ||9||
10. O friend, He is satisfied without any food - all joys wait upon Him in service. ||10||
11. O friend, He has neither birth nor death - He who created them both. ||11||
12. O friend, let His glory be sung - let us praise the power and qualities of Hari. ||12||
13. O friend, He is the father of all - yet He Himself has no mother or father. ||13||
14. O friend, He is the master of all - and He has no master over Him. ||14||
15. O friend, He is above all - and above Him nothing has been created. ||15||
16. O friend, He has no equal - what comparison, then, can I give for Him? ||16||
17. O friend, by Him the world is driven on - tormented in the wildfire of delusion. ||17||
18. O friend, with form and without form, endless - however much one tells of Him, He cannot be told. ||18||
19. O friend, He whom the Vedas do not fathom - hard even for the mind of the lord of yogis to reach. ||19||
20. O friend, knowing this, serve Him always - You alone ever are; I am not. ||20||
21. O friend, in this way efface the self - serve the Father, and He will remember you. ||21||
22. O friend, day and night I bow to Him - day and night I repeat [the Name of] the Supreme Brahman. ||22||
23. O friend, at the last hour the soul remains - dragged by its karma it wanders through the ages. ||23||
24. O friend, the soul is broken by delusion - [so] lust, anger and pride are cast away. ||24||
25. O friend, You alone are free of fear - deeds done [in You] do not cling. ||25||
26. O friend, almighty Creator - the karma written on the head must be borne. ||26||
27. O friend, for the sake of establishing dharma (right order) - He came down in a single portion of Himself. ||27||
28. O friend, [it was] for the good of others - incomparable are Your deeds. ||28||
29. O friend, You have no work of Your own to do - in You there is no attachment, hatred or pride. ||29||
30. O friend, no fault is in You - the King does whatever He wills. ||30||

[Thus ends Shri Heli, complete ||4||]

[Here begins Shri Saheli ||5||. Every verse carries the refrain "saheldi re" - "O dear friend".]

1. Let us sing of that Supreme Self - O dear friend - the great One, the treasury of all virtues. ||1||
2. By remembrance of His Name - O dear friend - the soul is released from this world. ||2||
3. In whatever manner He holds His own being - O dear friend - in that same way He holds the life-breath [of all]. ||3||
4. The purpose for which You set all this in motion - O dear friend - You alone, the all-knowing, know it. ||4||
5. With ease You created Brahma the ordainer and Shiva - O dear friend - gods and men are hardly worth the mention. ||5||
6. He who is the support of all - O dear friend - how could we ever let go of such a Father? ||6||
7. Wounded, the soul cries out - O dear friend - listen, Supreme Self, O Father. ||7||
8. I was made to leave Your nearness - O dear friend - what was my offence? ||8||
9. Why was the happiness of home forgotten - O dear friend - why was I lost here in this forest? ||9||
10. How long have I been tormented - O dear friend - at the hands of the enemies, lust and its kin. ||10||
11. In this forest the wildfire of greed is burning - O dear friend - and Death the hunter roams here at his sport. ||11||
12. Maya (illusion) was let loose as the decoy doe - O dear friend - and the net of karma was spread. ||12||
13. Caught in the net I am now helpless - O dear friend - the soul, infatuated, has lost its senses. ||13||
14. It has no memory of what went before or comes after - O dear friend - it has no awareness of its own self. ||14||
15. Gods and men writhe in that net - O dear friend - all who have been given bodies. ||15||
16. While it is still forming, [the body] is cut off - O dear friend - broken in the womb itself. ||16||
17. Take a body, and the happiness you obtain - O dear friend - is [like] scalding oil being pressed out. ||17||
18. One never points to one's own fault - O dear friend - the fault that lies within oneself. ||18||
19. Time devours [us] daily, bit by bit - O dear friend - and still the self does not wake. ||19||
20. Into such great sorrow have I been cast - O dear friend - now take care of me, Father. ||20||
21. By the Name break [the round of] this body - O dear friend - by remembrance remove its corruptions. ||21||
22. Make what is Yours like Yourself - O dear friend - take me now, delay no longer. ||22||

[Thus ends Shri Saheli, complete ||5||]

sections.title_en: Ghodli - 'the little mare', a song in galloping metre
sections.translation:
[Here begins Shri Ghodli ||6||. Every verse opens with the word "ghodli" (the little mare), the name of the tune, repeated as "gho." in the printed refrain.]

1. Meditation has fastened on the Supreme Brahman; pride, envy and arrogance are cast off; the refuge of Hari has been gained. ||1||
2. The world has been made empty [to me]; unbroken meditation has arisen. ||2||
3. I have met Him who is beyond the three gunas (the three qualities of nature); the company of the qualities has been left behind. ||3||
4. The sun of knowledge has risen; the night of maya has passed away. ||4||
5. The moon of the mind has become spotless; the cloud of delusion has lifted. ||5||
6. Delusion has passed like the winter; the spring of devotion to Vishnu has come. ||6||
7. Through remembrance He has been found near; the sun of the mind has turned northward. ||7||
8. The mango tree of virtues has blossomed; the koel of longing has made its home there. ||8||
9. Supreme bliss has welled up; lust and its companions have burnt out like a Holi fire. ||9||
10. Dharma, contentment and discernment - in that very moment [all] takes on the splendour of the rains. ||10||
11. All other thoughts are broken; the waking mind has met the Supreme Brahman. ||11||
12. Him whom no one can fathom - serve that unfathomable One. ||12||
13. How can there be lasting liberation without remembering the Lord of liberation? ||13||
14. Hell and the dwelling in the womb are broken; coming and going [in rebirth] has been ended. ||14||
15. Endless are the forms in every vessel; by the Guru's word all become one. ||15||
16. Time has given up its claim; Yama (death) has let go and stands aside. ||16||
17. The gods give great honour; Yama's account [against me] has been set aside. ||17||
18. The Father has taken care of me; He removed the separateness and kept me near Him. ||18||
19. Know the manner of liberation: its unshakable happiness is very great indeed. ||19||
20. Without hands He fashions the universe; without feet He moves through all that moves and does not move. ||20||
21. Without a mouth He speaks the truth; without eyes He sees everything. ||21||
22. Without a stomach He takes His food; without senses He enjoys. ||22||
23. Without form He reigns; He shines without wearing any ornament. ||23||
24. Without desire He brings all being into play; ever in bliss He sports. ||24||
25. Without a mind He knows all; without ears He hears everything. ||25||
26. The soul takes on no [further] body; by that power it attains the Supreme Self. ||26||
27. Keep the lamp of remembrance burning; the occasions of maya and greed are many. ||27||
28. When the lamp stays [alight] within the house, then the soul's purpose is fulfilled. ||28||
29. Mansions and the affairs of the world - such happiness comes, and then is spoiled again. ||29||
30. I have left the impermanent world behind; I know the Supreme Self to be the one thing of worth. ||30||
31. Then there is no sorrow of birth and death; joyfully let us serve the Supreme Brahman. ||31||
32. Keep remembrance within you, by which the Lord of the earth is attained. ||32||
33. He made the self as though it were not; my mind has met the mind of the Father. ||33||
34. If meditation lasts to the very end, one attains the state of the Supreme Brahman. ||34||
35. This is what the devotee asks here: that separateness be wiped away and all become one. ||35||
36. Whoever listens to this with conviction attains that hard-won liberation with ease. ||36||

[Thus ends Shri Ghodli, complete ||6||]

Here begins the holy Vani ||7||

1. Parabrahma has wedded Vani (the divine Word); through the whole universe rings the cry of victory. The four sources of birth have been made pure; the delusion of worldly existence is broken.

2. The reckonings of Yama, lord of death, have been struck out; the trade of hell has been wound up. The bonds of living beings are loosed; all attain liberation this time round.

3. Freed are all things unmoving and moving; freed are gods, men and serpents. Freed are the seven sages and the nine planets; freed are the great munis (sages) of the world.

4. Hari, Har (Shiva) and Brahma rejoice; in house after house there is festival. The surge of gladness is very great; we shall sing of the bridegroom of Vani.

5. At every door festive banners fly up; the doorways are hung with garlands and festoons. The universe is filled with flowers and blossom; all six seasons wear joy.

6. Sprinklings of divine sandal-paste fall; the clouds of all twelve months rejoice. The Panchajanya conch is blown; the worlds resound with its unceasing roar.

7. Narayan, the lord of Lakshmi, rejoices greatly within his heart. Shankar dances the tandav; its sweep spreads out through all the worlds.

8. Ganga breaks loose from the crown; the serpent Vasuki sways. Eighty-eight thousand sages are in delight, and Brahma recites the Vedas.

9. So long as Parabrahma, the husband of Vani, remained unwed, so long there was affliction and bondage, and not once any happiness.

10. Now the whole universe has become happy, now that Jagannath has wed as befits him. Joy and supreme bliss have come; affliction and great sorrow are broken.

11. The hard sorrows are broken; the soul has become pure. The forms of the eighty-four lakh species -- all those entanglements are wholly broken.

12. The imagining of the three worlds is broken; there is one joy alone. Victory to the Supreme Self, Parabrahma; victory, victory to the support of the universe.

13. Crores of universes are the horses of the wedding train; in house after house the four auspicious wedding rounds. There is no day nor night nor hour, no moment, no age, no fraction of time, no world's end.

14. No hunger, no thirst, no sleep; no anxiety, no household drudgery. All that moves and moves not is satisfied; there is happiness, supreme bliss, rejoicing.

15. Nothing else is wanted; everyone's searching is at an end. Parabrahma the King is seated on his throne, and before him his beloved saints.

16. Let all do japa (repetition) of his virtues -- he who bears the four-armed form. No other name is to be spoken with the mouth; recite only "Ram".

17. There is no fear of birth, old age or death; there is no other business at all. You alone are the Lord of the earth; all the saints rejoice.

Here the Vani is complete ||7||

End of the first vishram (resting-point) of the five-day parayan (recitation).

Here begins the holy Aarti ||8||

1. Parabrahma, Padmanabh, Purushottam -- he stands in no lineage. Hari the unmanifest, Govind, is my thought. Take care of us, Shripati, our Lord.

2. Hari is four-armed and dark of hue, the beautiful bearer of the Sharang bow. Hari is the lovely King of Vaikunth, Damodar who destroys sin.

3. Hari is stainless and formless; let us worship that spotless Purush (Person). Let us sing of Hari, the King of Dwarka, dark-hued and beautiful.

4. Serve Hari, the all-capable essence, whose farther limit no one can reach. That same Hari is imperishable; the Lord grants a dwelling in Vaikunth.

5. Hari is Madhav, Mukund, Murari -- the beautiful great God. Hari is the giver of bhakti (devotion) and mukti (liberation); Narayan is stainless.

6. Ever the bearer of the Sharang bow, of gracious discernment; Kanhaiya who is beyond, the very Self. [unclear] -- the three worlds writhe in longing for you to carry them across.

7. The poor soul is infatuated within its own imaginings; in the Kali age the soul is struck down. Without Hari it finds not a moment's breath; [unclear] -- the Lord, bearer of the Sharang bow.

8. Ever is there eagerness in the Vaishnav's heart, joy surging through the body. Welcome, King Parabrahma! The Beloved has come to dwell among the Vaishnav folk.

9. Hari's cry of victory has spread everywhere; sweet indeed is the essential word now. Faith in Hari has entered the mind; the nooses of the four sources of birth are loosed.

10. Father, in home after home there is now the dwelling of Vaikunth; your servants make their plea. Welcome, King Parabrahma -- the saints have served the all-capable Lord.

Here the holy Aarti is complete ||8||

Here begins the holy Bidu ||9||

1. Let us praise King Parabrahma; Gopal dwells in the lotus of the heart. Let us not set the Name aside for even an instant -- let time be spent in just this way.

2. Let us resort to the company of saints as to the Ganga; the thousand names are our gopichandan (sacred clay mark) and tulsi. Let us bathe daily in that Triveni confluence -- let us resort to the company of saints as to the Ganga.

3. Where there is no "I" and no "mine" -- that is the city of liberation, that alone is the true Kashi. Those who abide in this inner state are freed from the sorrow of dwelling in the womb. (refrain: Let us resort to the company of saints...)

4. The night of imagining is hard to bear; in the sleep of maya an age has been slept away. Joy and grief are both but dreams -- so wakes the discernment of true knowledge. (refrain)

5. For those whom Shri Padmanabh has awakened, the night has passed into dawn. They have left off both sleep and dream -- thus has the sun of Parabrahma risen. (refrain)

6. The sun that is Parabrahma burns forever; there night never comes even once. Day and night your remembrance goes on -- thus the darkness of delusion has passed away. (refrain)

7. Brahma and the rest, Shiva the primordial, Indra and the others, the sun and the moon -- all of them ever tremble at the fear of death; your saints alone are fearless. (refrain)

8. Thus has Shri Padmanabh spoken: this alone is the discernment of true knowledge. He taught the thousand names; the mantra of Hari is the essence of all. (refrain)

Here the holy Bidu is complete ||9||

Here begin the holy Kadvas ||1|| ||10||

1. Hari, Hari -- lovely is bhakti (devotion) to Parabrahma; ascetics, sages and gods long for it. Unless it is granted, how can anyone obtain it?

2. Hari, Hari -- the soul has taken birth through crores of existences; without Hari it finds no farther shore. Through the company of saints, Hariji is found.

3. Hari, Hari -- follow the all-capable Parabrahma; the greatest doubt is broken. All fears are now crushed.

4. Hari, Hari -- the soul, held in another's power, was tormented; then Hari Parabrahma was served. Brahma, Har (Shiva) and the rest came under his sway.

Aad (opening) ||1||

1. Hari is beyond the reach of Hari, Har and Brahma themselves; he is the guru of all that moves and moves not. Great is that formless Lord.

2. Hari is dear to the sages headed by Sanak; he is exceedingly hard to attain, the support of crores of universes.

3. Hari is dark as a rain-cloud in the sky, and utterly pure -- the child, the darling of the Yadu clan.

4. Hari is the lovely Kanhaiya, beautiful and delightful; Gopal plays in joyous sport.

Aad (opening) ||2||

1. Gopal the stainless plays and plays in joy -- his body dark as collyrium.

2. Hari is the life of the world, unfathomable, unborn; the Yadav hero, the enemy of worldly existence.

3. Hari, the Yadav hero, ferries one across the ocean of existence -- and that same one grazes the cows as a cowherd boy.

4. Sweet is Hari's voice; with its sweet strain it enchants the three worlds. Brahma and the rest cannot find its limit.

Aad (opening) ||3||

1. Parabrahma, supreme bliss; the Lord, treasury of virtues, the Govind of the gopis. He is the delight of the Yadavs; Hari is bowed to by the three worlds. (This verse is printed twice, at the turn of the page.)

2. All-capable and exceedingly mighty; the Lord, unmanifest, one and endless. Beyond the reach of the gods; Hari is boundless, past both Hari and Har.

3. He has taken hold of many universes; Lord, you alone, Hari, pervade all. He sports, and yet stands apart; that Hari no one has seen.

4. From the beginning his form is unmanifest; the Lord's own nature is Hari, Har and Brahma. Of himself he unfolds; Hari extends through the three worlds.

Aad (opening) ||4||

1. Supreme Person, Supreme Self, father of the soul; Vasudev, Hari, Parabrahma, lord of Brahma and Maheshwar.

2. In yourself you are unmanifest, yet you have made your incarnations manifest. Brahma and the other gods, men and demons, cannot reach your limit.

3. Shuk, Sanak and the rest serve him -- the one incomparable God. Many are the forms that are his, and many are their names.

4. He has beguiled all that moves and moves not, and led thought astray in many ways. Driven by the qualities of prakriti (nature), the soul wanders infatuated through the world.

5. Pervading all things moving and unmoving, he has given them into the hand of Time. The anguish and sorrow of the womb; the bad deeds and the good go along with the soul.

6. The soul is subject to birth and death, ignorant of knowledge of the Self. Giving it the essential word, he established the Vedas and Puranas.

7. One inner path has been taken up; without the Lord there is no higher knowledge. Leaving aside all the lords of the earth, I have set myself in unwavering meditation.

8. Lord, you alone are, there is no other; there is no one at all in this whole world. [unclear] -- this cruel round; ward off, O Lord, rebirth in the womb.

Aad (opening) ||5||

1. Gods and sages in the sky sing the praise of Gokul; Hari is utterly beyond understanding. Hari, Hari -- Govind plays, filled with joy.

2. Playing himself, he makes the cowherd boys play; Hari plays and makes others play. Hari eats and makes others eat. Brahma and the rest ponder Hari in the heavens.

(Continuing Kadvun 1, Aad 6)

3. The Inscrutable One set his play afoot in Gokul -- a play that Brahma and the other gods long for. Hari himself touches all and yet is untouched by any of it.

4. Brahma, who carried off the calves, was left thwarted; the elder cowherd Hari is himself the maker of all. Hari, Hari -- in mere sport he fashions crores of universes.

Aad (opening) ||6||

1. The colour has taken, oh the colour has taken -- Lord, in meditation on Parabrahma; having looked at the path of rites, I have let it go.

2. It is not there, ah, it is not there -- what essence did I ever gain from it? No farther shore of worldly existence is to be seen.

3. The mind was steeped in love many a time before -- in son, in wife, in wealth, in youth.

4. All of that perishes, all of that perishes; every one of those pleasures is empty. Seeing this, the colour faded away.

Aad (opening) ||7||

1. Supreme Self, oh Supreme Self -- Lord, you are Parabrahma; you it was who created Brahma and Maheshwar.

2. You are your own, oh you are your own -- Lord, all this is yours in every age; now look to what is ours.

3. All of it, ah all of it -- in this fashion you spread yourself abroad; of your own self you became the Unmanifest.

4. You are the great one, oh you are the great one -- such is the support of the ages; if [your own] must suffer sorrow, does that not shame you?

Aad (opening) ||8||

Here the first Kadvun is complete ||1||

Here begins the second Kadvun ||2||

1. Hari, Hari -- Kanha, lord of crores of universes, the great king of the Yadavs; him the Vedas and Upanishads sing.

2. Hari, Hari -- the sages who worshipped him with oblations: the knowing ones he made unknowing; when he stood before them asking, only then was he recognised.

3. Hari, Hari -- the women recognised him as the Purusha of the sacrifice; the unknowing he made knowing, and to them he gave the supreme state.

4. Hari, Hari -- he gladdened his teacher Sandipani, that Lord who is a wondrous giver; from him the guru asked back his dead son [as his fee].

Aad (opening) ||1||

1. Hari lifted the hill of Govardhan upon his hand; he is the uplifter of the age -- remembrance of the endless God.

2. Hari it is who stirs the hearts of loving women, exceedingly beautiful; on him Dhruv, Shuk and Narad set their thought.

3. The gods stand at the gate of Hari's Vaikunth; though they gaze, they do not attain it; the great sages enter within.

4. Hari's saints, filled with bliss, sport in happiness; they follow close after him; theirs is the rule of the fearless realm.

Aad (opening) ||2||

1. Hari, Hari -- the company of the saints: keep that satsang (holy company) night and day, and drink the supreme bliss.

2. Birth and death depart, they depart; there is no fear of coming again into the world -- a place beyond the reach of gods, sages and Indra.

3. Take refuge in Hari -- he who releases the caged soul, the ocean of compassion, the giver of riches and of the imperishable state.

4. Hari, Hari -- Dhruv, Prahlad and Vibhishan he made unshakable; unmoving is his grace upon his devotees.

Aad (opening) ||3||

1. As fire is one, Lord, and from it many lamps are lit; the fire is exceedingly strong -- the lamp, Hari, has not that strength.

2. That fire is Parabrahma, Lord; the lamps are Hari, Har and Brahma, gods, men and serpents -- everything that stands still and everything that moves.

3. Great is he, the support of the ages, Lord, whose limit is never found; he who took sixteen thousand brides -- that Hari; and great are Brahma and Shankar.

4. Let the soul abide in meditation on Hari; Lord, do not take prakriti (material nature) to be your own self. Parabrahma is unmanifest; all that moves serves Hari.

5. The soul is in your hand, Lord; it does not belong with prakriti. Without Hari I have wandered through crores of births; now I have come to follow, taking refuge in Hari.

Aad (opening) ||4||

1. Having been born into a body, how can you ask for happiness? You are already in the hands of your enemies. The objects of sense do not release you for an instant; death walks beside you every moment.

2. Blind in the midst of the pleasures you live among -- brother, you are falling into ruin. In your folly you do not wake; you will suffer sorrow to the very end.

3. You alone were before creation; you, Hari, are the maker of all. You alone are great and all-capable; you, Hari, are the treasury of compassion.

4. To the servant who serves you, you are merciful; to the man without devotion you are Death itself. I am tormented, in the grip of karma and the senses; now set this wretched one free.

5. You are Krishna, Govind, Murari -- carry this soul across. You are Hari, Purushottam, Parabrahma, Vishnu, Narayan.

6. Dark as the rain-cloud, robed in yellow silk, endlessly lovely of form; lotus-eyed and lotus-faced, husband of the daughter of the lord of the waters [Lakshmi].

7. Those who came to him even in enmity -- their purpose too he accomplished. Those who followed him in the mood of bhakti (devotion) -- give them now the unshakable abode.

8. Spotless, inscrutable, incomparable -- no comparison for him can be spoken. Lord of the world, supreme God; meditate on that Ishwar night and day.

Aad (opening) ||5||

1. Devoted to his devotees, upholder of dharma -- that Hari is Nand's own child. Hari, Hari -- the enemies of the saints he ground down; Hari cast them from their place.

2. Ravan and the rest were set up by Har and the other gods, and Hari himself again set [his devotee] in that place; Hari is the support of his devotees.

3. In Vrindavan the support of the ages sports with the gopis, and is yet the true brahmachari (celibate); Hari is himself the master of the three worlds.

4. When the waters came flooding, he kept Gokul safe; Hari's play broke the rain-clouds apart; Hari is the giver of liberation.

Aad (opening) ||6||

1. The colour has taken, oh the colour has taken -- Lord, the fast crimson of madder; the fleeting safflower dye has washed away.

2. I have known it for poison, known it for poison -- the delight of lust that I found; all enjoyments are like fire.

3. Let it go now, let it go now -- I have found the world to be sorrow; dispassion I have embraced as my brother.

4. That has swept it away, that has swept it away -- I have seen through the fellowship of passion [unclear]; lust, anger and pride I have cast off.

Aad (opening) ||7||

1. Hari Govinda, oh Hari Govinda -- Lord, you are Parabrahma; begging your grace I make my prayer.

2. This little game, this little game -- set it aside now; in the power of others I have suffered sorrows.

3. This is our own, this is our own -- Lord, the very form of the Self; why then do you make them separate and set them rolling about?

4. You have spread yourself out, you have spread yourself out -- exceedingly clever and all-knowing; alone you sport within the four mines of birth.

Aad (opening) ||8||

Here the second Kadvun is complete ||2||

Here begins the third Kadvun ||3||

1. Hari, Hari -- let us praise the ornament of the Yadu line, he who drained Putana dry; who snapped the twin Arjun trees as he was dragged along.

2. Hari, Hari -- the cart-demon and Trinavart and all the rest he slew; he took to his play in Gokul; Dhenuk and Vatsasur he killed.

3. Hari, Hari -- great were the festivities in Gokul; he mastered the serpent Kaliya; mounted upon the serpent my Lord danced.

4. Hari, Hari -- Akrur recognised him as Parabrahma; he was brought into the midst of the wrestlers; the whole clan of Kans he destroyed.

5. Hari, Hari -- Indra and the other gods rejoiced in heart; he fulfilled the longings of his devotees' hearts; yet the Lord has no work of his own to do.

Aad (opening) ||1||

1. Hari, Hari -- as is the moon's radiance on the autumn full-moon night, such is the radiance of his face; his eyes are like lotuses.

2. Hari's lips put the bimb fruit to shame -- it counts for nothing beside them; his teeth are lovely as rubies.

3. Gazing on the savour of Hari's beauty, greatly delighted, the women can find no end of it.

4. Hari, smiling a faint smile, slew the foe; in him there is no anger, no envy, no pride.

Aad (opening) ||2||

1. Hari, Hari -- Kalayavan was a demon of great might, known throughout the world of men.

2. Hari, Hari -- lord of three and twenty legions was he; and that lord's might Hari overcame.

3. Hari, Hari -- Shri Krishna took land from the sea and made his capital there.

4. Hari, Hari -- in a single night, and no one knew of it, he brought Mathura's people there.

Aad (opening) ||3||

1. He brought them, he brought Mathura's people there; no one knows the manner of Hari's doing. Great are the fort and the temples; as Hari wills, so it is.

2. The city stood empty, Hari alone within it; there came army upon army; they ringed the city round, and there they saw Hari alone.

3. The demon spoke out boldly, knowing nothing of Hari's strength; he demanded battle; and the foe pressed on ahead of Hari.

4. Hari saw that the foe was a fool: who would fight with such a one? The Lord of the worlds walked away, and the enemy ran on toward his own death.

5. Where Muchukand lay sleeping, into that cave went Govind; the king awoke, and that very instant the lord of the demons fell.

Aad (opening) ||4||

1. The lord of all the worlds is one alone; the king sports without a body. Meditate on that Hari, Parabrahma -- inscrutable, unborn, the hero.

2. Parabrahma, you are not without pity; hear this small prayer of mine. The soul falling into the womb suffers great pain -- put an end to it.

3. The soul is one, and it is yours; why then does it do these separate deeds? Make all that moves and moves not one; devotion to Vishnu is its own true dharma.

4. Without bhakti (devotion) to Hari, in ignorance, no one grasps your secret. On the one hand a man reaps the deeds already done; on the other he goes on gathering deeds still.

5. Bound in so great a chain of affliction -- why, Father, have you overlooked it? Laying the whole matter on the head of karma, the scriptures have let it go.

6. If a man wears out the old deeds by living them through and refuses to make new ones -- if in this way he becomes free of karma -- then release would come to him at once.

7. So long as even one deed remains, birth is not escaped; to reap it he is made to take a body and to bear many blows from Yama's men.

8. While one wears a body there is no freedom from karma; yet I will not let go of Hari's name. By the refuge of the Name I shall reach freedom from karma, and final release.

Aad (opening) ||5||

1. He creates gods, men and serpents, and he destroys them; Hari it is who wards off unrighteousness. Hari, Hari -- the master of the three worlds sets dharma in its place.

2. His drama no one understands; Hari alone understands himself; his ways are past all understanding.

3. From the beginning the formless One composes many dramas; Hari brings forth many forms; and alone, all by himself, he watches and watches.

4. Having set gods and demons against each other, he stood apart though he was within it; Hari drives the three worlds. No one grasps the pulling of Hari's strings.

Aad (opening) ||6||

1. The remembrance of Hari, the remembrance of Hari -- that is the inexhaustible treasury; and yet [unclear] he became a pauper.

2. He has suffered, he has suffered, in the midst of the four mines of birth -- all for not knowing of that treasury.

3. He showed it, he showed it -- the holy Guru showed the treasury, whose form is the remembrance of Parabrahma.

4. By that it was broken, by that it was broken -- the helplessness of birth after birth, which is the very shape of the pain of dwelling in the womb.

Aad (opening) ||7||

1. Supreme Self, oh Supreme Self -- Lord, endless God; you became a light no bigger than a thumb.

2. Most mighty, oh most mighty -- Lord, the maker of all; why then follow after feeble prakriti (material nature)?

3. This soul, this soul -- Lord, it arose out of you; between you and it there is no separation.

4. This soul, this soul -- Lord, undo its distress; before you there is no other.

Aad (opening) ||8||

Here the third Kadvun is complete ||3||

|| Here begins the holy Kadavu ||4||

1. Hari, Hari — Kanhan (Krishna) of dark hue, let us sing of him: a broad tilak of musk upon his brow. The child is beautiful, exceedingly lovely. ||1||
2. Hariji's golden crown is charming; rubies beyond counting are set in it; diamonds flash there like the sun. ||2||
3. In Hariji's ears are earrings, at his throat a neck-band; upon his breast a garland of pearls; the garland with the Kaustubh gem blazes. ||3||
4. A pearl sways at Hariji's nose; jewelled bangles are on his hands; gem-studded armlets upon his arms. ||4||
5. Hariji wears a yellow silken robe; sandal paste is smeared on his breast; garlands and flower-tufts, blossoms in plenty. ||5||

|| Aad ||1||

1. Hari outwitted King Ambarish; he came down in incarnation as the occasion required — the Lord, in all ten avatars. ||1||
2. Hari stood at the door of Bali; though Bali looked, he did not grasp him — he who is beyond, the Lord of yogis. ||2||
3. Hari filled Sudama with riches — that supremely resourceful one; Sudama recognized in him the treasure-house of liberation. ||3||
4. Hari — perishable riches he did not embrace; he made everything steadfast, and took the witness of [unclear]. ||4||

|| Aad ||2||

1. Hari, Hari — say "Krishna, Krishna": Rukmini, night and day, is dyed in the virtues of Gopal. ||1||
2. Hari, Hari — he fulfilled the heart's longing of her, and crushed King Shishupal. ||2||
3. Hari, Hari — sixteen thousand maidens lay in prison; Narakasur had seized their very lives. ||3||
4. Hariji slew the demon and set the maidens free — the wielder of the discus (Chakrapani), who loves his devotees. ||4||

|| Aad ||3||

1. Pure and supreme knowledge; the Lord, the treasury of qualities and arts; a purifying place of pilgrimage — holy is the kirtan (hymn) of Hari. ||1||
2. The radiance of ten million suns; the Lord upholds the earth and the sky; victory, victory to Vishvambhar, the sustainer of all — Hari, who is terror to the demons. ||2||
3. Hari, the Supreme Self, Ram, whose Name is spotless for ever; the deliverer of the three worlds — Hari, who wards off hell. ||3||
4. The Great Death of death itself; the Lord Gopal who burns away sin; the beloved of Tulsi — Hari, hard to attain even for gods and men. ||4||

|| Aad ||4||

1. O Lord, you are the almighty father: avert this calamity. The little soul has been ruined by vain imagining — remove that first of all. ||1||
2. The blame lies upon the head of karma, but the matter is in your hands; unceasing remembrance of you breaks apart the whole mass of karma. ||2||
3. Driven by karma the soul has wandered and fled, into ever-new wombs without number — happy or wretched, highest or middling, all are the Lord's own servants. ||3||
4. Truly it heaps up new karma while it endures the old — thus there is no crossing beyond karma; but if you show your grace now, then this very moment there is release. ||4||
5. Thakor, you alone are father, you are brother, treasury of compassion; I am an offender destitute of your bhakti (devotion) — forgive me, Lord Govind, Kanhan. ||5||
6. Those whom you have saved before — great were their offences, yet all of them now sport in supreme bliss, because you, the almighty king, were pleased with them. ||6||
7. Now there is no fear of prakriti (material nature); I have served Kanhan of Gokul; my mind is absorbed in the contemplation of pure consciousness; the Name of Hari has burnt my karma away. ||7||
8. You are the master of my soul and my mind — I am not its master, not for a moment; take back your own possession into your keeping, for with me it is spoiled beyond measure. ||8||

|| Aad ||5||

1. Brahma spoke to Dharmaraj: do not open a quarrel with the great, do not utter unrighteousness — the Vaishnavas are Hari's own, and worthy of worship. ||1||
2. He on whose mouth is the nectar of Hari's Name, tulsi at his throat and gopichandan on his forehead — gods and men bow to him; Brahma declares him the pilgrimage-place of pilgrimage-places. ||2||
3. Even those who perform the worship of Shankar and the rest — that very instant they leave off from there, and come and fix their attention where the Vaishnava folk are: so Brahma declares. ||3||
4. Serve such an almighty one, devoted to his bhaktas and doing good to others; he alone is the stainless God (Niranjan); serve him, for he destroys the anguish of the womb. ||4||

|| Aad ||6||

1. O Hari, my Lord, O Hari, my Lord — Father, take care of me; this soul is in the power of birth and death. ||1||
2. Forgetting, forgetting — the Name of Hari, the Parbrahm; with an unheeding mind I have gone blind. ||2||
3. O Hari, my Lord, O my Lord — you are compassionate to the lowly; do not so forget this poor wretch. ||3||
4. Many, so many have I done — deeds done for my own sake; and hell and Yama are fearsome. ||4||
5. Exceedingly hard, exceedingly hard — great torments before this; in earlier births I have endured them. ||5||
6. In dread of that, in dread of that, O Lord, this soul has come to take refuge in you. ||6||
7. Now keep me, now keep me, Lord, within your own self; honour the word you yourself have given. ||7||

|| Aad ||7||

1. Hari, Parbrahm — Hari, Parbrahm — Lord, you are the Supreme Brahman; by good fortune I have obtained your japa (repetition of the Name). ||1||
2. Hari, the One alone — Hari, the One alone — Lord, fulfil my longing; may bhakti spring up in all that moves and all that moves not. ||2||
3. Set it up thus, set it up thus, Lord — an age of Vaikunth; in house after house let there be no other talk. ||3||
4. He has taken birth, he has taken birth — Kanhan of Gokul, Shri Padmanabh, Purushottam. ||4||
5. Whoever sings, whoever listens to this song bound upon Parbrahm — for him the bonds of worldly existence are loosed. ||5||

|| Aad ||8||

|| Thus the Kadavu is complete ||4||10

The second resting-place (vishram) of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.

|| Here begins the holy Vadikaraj ||11||

1. There, neither the existent nor the non-existent is; there is neither the formless nor form; there neither wind nor sky is; there is neither the light of the ages nor darkness. ||1||
2. Time has devoured human beings, demons, gods, sages and the great siddhas; it has devoured the sixty-four yoginis, the shaktis, Shikotar, and countless crores besides. ||2||
3. It has devoured the eighty-four chetaks (attendant spirits) and the fifty-two mighty Virs; foremost and greatest of all is that Almighty, the imperceptible Parbrahm, the king. ||3||
4. He it is who created Mahakal — at whose Name death itself dies; he established Brahma, Har and the rest; there is no end to the universes. ||4||
5. In his play he makes the existent non-existent — gods and men, many times over. ||5||

|| Valan (refrain) ||

6. Many times over he creates gods and men; he establishes Brahma, Har and the rest; the Almighty by his lila shapes the ages, and cuts down the demons and the wicked. ||6||
7. Heaven, the mortal world, the netherworld — the three worlds; he lays out the earth and the sky; taking many forms he upholds dharma, and casts off the qualities of prakriti (material nature). ||6|| [the printed number 6 is repeated here]
8. That Hari, the Parbrahm who is the Supreme Brahman — Lord Padmanabhji, I take refuge in you. ||8||

|| Aad ||1||

1. Remember Narayan first of all — the great one, the giver of liberation; great in his majesty is the Lord of Lakshmi, the four-armed king, Lord of the three worlds. ||1||
2. He reclined upon the ocean of milk, to cut off the race of the demons; he establishes universes by the crore — sages, men, and pure souls. ||2||

|| Valan ||

3. Sages, men and pure souls, O Lord — Shuk, Sanak and the rest sport there; the Guru and his like, Maheshwar, Indra and the rest — not one of them finds his farther shore. ||3||
4. Universe upon universe, Brahmas and Hars — many and separate, he establishes them all; the end of the universes is not to be found; who then can give the end of Him? ||4||
5. That Hari, the Parbrahm who is the Supreme Brahman — Lord Padmanabhji, I take refuge in you. ||5||

|| Aad ||2||

1. First, to destroy Shankhasur, he took birth in the midst of the ocean; the Lord assumed the form of a fish — his lila in the midst of the waters. ||1||
2. In play he tossed up his tail; the ocean was flung to the sky; in that water Meru was drowned, and the sun, the moon, the sea and the world of the gods. ||2||
3. As a hawk falls upon a dove, he swooped and slew the demon Shankhasur; he blew the five-fold conch; in the three worlds there was festival, and the drums of victory. ||3||

|| Valan ||

4. In the three worlds the festival is unceasing, and terror falls upon the demons; Brahma came there bearing his offering, and with his four mouths recites the four Vedas. ||4||
5. There he uprooted the demons' whole line, and established gods and men in security; the Vedas that had gone to the demon race he gave back to Brahma, lineage by lineage. ||5||
6. That Hari, the Parbrahm who is the Supreme Brahman — Lord Padmanabhji, I take refuge in you. ||6||

|| Aad ||3||

1. Sporting in the form of the Tortoise, he bore Mount Mandar upon his back; as Mandar turned it felt pleasant, and sleep came upon the Tortoise there. ||1||
