2. Fourteen jewels were drawn out from there; Lakshmi serves the feet of Hari; gods, demons, men and sages sing his praise; his form is vaster than the great mountain. ||2||

|| Valan ||

3. Mountainous and mighty is that form, O Lord; as the Tortoise he took his second incarnation; Sheshnag the bearer of the earth was upheld, and upon the portion of his back they were saved. ||3||
4. Mandar was held fast, the gods churned the deep, and the fourteen jewels were taken there; in this way Narayan, who loves his devotees, accomplished every purpose of the gods. ||4||
5. That Hari, the Parbrahm who is the Supreme Brahman — Lord Padmanabhji, I take refuge in you. ||5||

|| Aad ||4||

|| Thus Shri Vadi Karaj is complete ||11||

(In the community of the Uda bhaktas it is said that the individual soul is ginned like cotton by the wheel of the world's joys and sorrows. This poem gives the instruction of the path of surrender by which one escapes from that. For this reason the poem has been given the name Lodhi Karaj — "the ginning rite".)

|| Here begins the holy Lodhi Karaj ||12||

1. Maya, like the goddess Shikotar, has seized the soul; it has been loaded with unclean spells and poisons and the like — take refuge in Hari, the Parbrahm king. ||1||
2. To avert the womb there is no other means — take refuge in Hari, the Parbrahm king. ||2||
3. In the Name of Parbrahm complete the great circle of worship; by remembrance call upon Narsinh and Vir. ||3||
4. By the Name of Parbrahm accomplish the great mantra; bind the mind steady, together with the senses. ||4||
5. Where there is no earth, no water, no sky, no wind, no fire — there too you alone are, my Lord, the one Parbrahm. ||5||
6. Within prakriti (nature), moving and unmoving, you set the jiva (individual soul); and to torment it in hell you gave the power into Yama's hand. ||6||
7. Through the soul you cause karma to be done; and to undergo that karma you cause a body to be taken. ||7||
8. In the power of birth and death the soul has been ruined; stung and filled with pain [unclear], it did not cry out with your Name. ||8||
9. When you, Lord, lay upon the leaf of the banyan tree — tell me, where was the soul then? ||9||
10. Your worthless devotee makes his petition with folded hands: meet me now, and release me from this anguish. ||10||

|| Thus Shri Lodhi Karaj is complete ||12||

Here begins Shri Harakh Bhavan ||13||

1. Shri Padmanabh became incarnate through yoga, and the name of Parbrahm was made manifest. The soul was freed from its great affliction and attains the abode of Vaikunth.

2. Do this, O Parbrahm King - almighty is this leela (divine play) of yours. The three worlds are as you are; victory, victory to you.

3. Gods, men and sages have taken hold of you; almighty Vishnu is their support. Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshwar do not reach the far edge of you.

4. You held your friend Sudama as your equal and made him a mansion beyond compare - the riches of ten million Indras in each single pillar.

5. In Gokul, Govind became incarnate, and the Lord [appeared] at Pindara. Attend upon him who loves his devotees; the saints perform your service.

6. In the beginning and from beginninglessness you alone are, and apart from you there is no other. Vishwambhar, you have spread through all; that same One is present in everything, without break.

7. Men and women utter the name of Parbrahm, and that too is by the grace of Parbrahm. Shri Padmanabh became incarnate through yoga - you are the king of Vaikunth.

8. You are Govind, Krishna, Morari, and Narayan and Ram. Wherever and in whatever form a devotee sets his mind, there is your abode.

9. You became incarnate in the ten avatars, beginning with the Fish and the rest. You redeemed all the demons and made an end of their curses.

10. You came in the Krishna avatar; I cannot reach the end of your qualities and deeds. Through the vision of the saints we know you - your forms are without limit.

11. You established the five elements, and mind, intellect, consciousness and ego. Joined with maya you spread through all - this is the manifest seat of the Purush (the primal Being).

12. You are attended by the five and the five again; the six and the two are your own form. Endless universes do you service - your true form is unmanifest.

13. I have heard of your forms in the Vedas, the shastras and the Puranas. For that reason I make my plea to you - you are the all-knowing King.

14. I entreat you, lover of your devotees, resting-place of devoted souls. Whoever serves you with a single mind attains your abode.

15. Know him as having form and as formless too; by his Name he carries [us] across. Utter the name Narayan - look and take hold of the essence.

16. You recline at ease upon Shesh, and Lakshmi serves your feet. We know you as the primal Vishnu, king of endless universes.

17. Brahma dwells in the lotus of your navel, yet even he does not know your far edge. Through meditation and through bhakti (devotion) you are known - you whose seat is the ocean of milk.

18. You fill the body and the universe as a pot stands filled within water. All serve you, beginning with Shambhu (Shiva).

19. As the face seen in a mirror is only a reflection, so, looking rightly, know this: you dwell in all things, without a break.

20. We know you as of endless form, and the universes are your body. The serpent-world dwells at your feet - you are the almighty sovereign.

21. Your way is a way of grace, and the Vaishnav people know it. Whoever serves you with a single mind, you take away their sorrows.

22. You are Padmanabh, you are Parbrahm, you are the great King. Great is your way - the saints rejoice, seventy-one [generations] with them.

23. The whole world, moving and unmoving, is enchanted, and Vishnu's devotees are full of joy. In house after house Vaikunth is set up - you are the almighty King.

24. Remain absorbed in the divine play; through bhakti, Hari is Parbrahm. Whoever repeats "Parbrahm" in this way attains your refuge.

25. Serve Hari Narayan the Lord together with Lakshmi. Your bhakti spreads wide; it wards off [ruin] and ferries [the soul] across to redemption.

26. The devotee serves in gladness, and the Lord is devoted to his devotees. To utter "Namo Vishnu" - this itself is your service.

27. And again we meditate on you with form - four-armed, dark of hue. You are Govind, Krishna, Morari; great are your names.

28. And again you are especially near, seen through knowledge of the Self. You dwell in the lotus of the heart; there is nothing equal to that.

29. Know that One in his special aspect: his form is full of light. Set aside the vessel, its oil and its ghee; the darkening soot is removed of itself.

30. All pilgrimages and vows are accomplished if one repeats the name of Parbrahm, bears gopichandan (sacred clay marking) on the head, and offers worship with tulsi among the saints.

31. Good is your bhakti, and whoever is wise knows it. Follow the path of the Veda; mighty is your command.

32. Without bhakti he is not attained; by bhakti the guileless King is won. Do not go searching again and again elsewhere - there is no other means.

33. Listen, all you devoted people, and do him service day and night. Take support of him in the mind's meditation - wherever you look, there is God.

34. To the eye each person seems separate, yet the moving and unmoving world is that same One - as the sun, standing in itself, is seen differently in each vessel [of water].

35. Considering further and looking closely, one knows the Self by the Self. In his own manner he became one [with him]; when the "I" is removed, you remain, O Father.

36. Before you, what is mine? All forms are yours. You set up the moon and the sun, O sovereign of the moving and unmoving world.

37. In satsang (holy company) happiness is found; repeat the name of the primal Mukund. He himself stands spread through endless universes - Govind.

38. Search as they may, the gods and Brahma and their worlds do not find your end. The Vedas declare "neti, not this"; to call oneself a knower is empty.

39. The base man does not understand this way and speaks with great pride; in his cleverness he will not believe, and the body has no substance.

40. He understands your way who gives up self-interest and lust, who sets his mind upon your feet and takes refuge in you, O Ram.

41. Without the great One there is no release - remember Shri Gopal. All the sages do him service; you are the protector of the saints.

42. Serve the Lord who rests on the couch of bliss, the imperishable King. The four aims of life are gained, and at the end an incomparable abode.

43. This soul has taken refuge in you, by the grace of the feet of the Vaishnavs. I have followed a simple-hearted bhakti - you are the almighty King.

44. Keep the company of the saints day and night, every watch and every moment, without blinking. Hold him in meditation and look, and your forms are seen.

45. Perform all the daily rites, each according to his family custom; worship in the many prescribed ways - in this manner one meets the Father.

46. In ignorance I played as I pleased and did not do your service. Show love and grace to this creature - you are the God of gods.

47. The soul is in your company, and so are mind, nature and light. Gazing into the lotus of the heart, I make my love for the Supreme Self.

48. The Lord dwells in all the worlds, and that same one is the King of liberation. Endless universes do him service, heaven foremost among them.

49. In meditation contemplate the Lord of the earth, the King who is without form. Devotees, do him service day and night; he takes you up and draws you close again.

50. So it is with the whole world, moving and unmoving: wherever you look, there is God. Make bhakti your very nature, and make an end of [binding] karma.

51. [unclear - the line on the devotee, karma and the scriptures is garbled in the source]; how then is the far shore reached? The soul is under the sway of prakriti (nature); its care now rests with you.

52. Bhakti has arisen through the moving and unmoving world - Lord, grant your grace. Let the whole universe become of one mind; let us contemplate the great King.

53. I hold this Harakh Bhavan (contemplation of joy) in my heart - look, look into the inquiry of the Self. Take up the repetition of the Name with understanding: the mantra of Hari is the essence of all.

Here ends Shri Harakh Bhavan ||13||

Here begins Shri Shok Bhavan ||14||

1. Hari, Parbrahm, you are the lord of virtue; everywhere you alone are. You are deathless and enjoy bliss, while sorrow falls upon the houses of others. Why is it so, O Lord, O great Father - you created the world, and with it suffering?

2. You laid suffering upon all and drove them on; driven along are gods, men, sages and yogis. Even the lords and kings of the heavenly worlds are subject to karma and to Time. Death has ruined the living creature - why is it so, O Lord?

3. Hari, Har and Brahma themselves weep - then of what account are others? Having given it a body you have made it suffer; and even now you do not take heed, O Father.

4. Sun, moon, ocean and earth, the nine planets and the garland of stars, all that is fixed and all that moves - you are all of it. Hold back Time, which devours it all.

5. You yourself have ruined your own [creation]; you have hidden away the knowledge of the Self. You yourself stay unmoved in bliss - what pride is this of yours?

6. By day he is driven by his business; the whole night goes in sleep. Doing just this he died, and fell into the hands of Yama's messengers.

7. The mind with no remembrance of Hari, the mouth without the name of Hari, the heart without devotion to Vishnu - his place is in hell.

8. Driven on by son, wife and wealth, he forgot the name of Hari. After death great suffering fell upon him; hell ruined the living creature.

9. He who always repeats Hari's name, who honours tulsi and the saints, who bears gopichandan (sacred clay marking) on his head - Time does not even come within his sight.

10. How the soul has been ruined - [worldly] ease makes one let go of Hari's name. By this ease all have been cheated; the world of delusion drives them along.

11. So long as he holds the body no thought of death comes to him. Suddenly Time devours him, and he wails without end.

12. The soul is made to leave the body; from that hour comes a time of pain. Bodiless, it is driven on in torment down a road hard and without end.

13. There is the terrifying forest of sword-leaves, where swords and arrows rain down; the sand burns with the colour of fire - and there the soul is driven.

14. Overhead twelve suns blaze, and the ground throws off scorching steam. The weeping soul is driven on - and you see it, O Merciful One.

15. Heavy blows fall from above; the road is fearfully dark. The ground is set with iron thorns; he cries out beyond measure.

16. Ahead flows the river Vaitarani, a hundred yojans wide; half of what it carries is blood and pus - and the soul is driven into it.

17. Tormented by hunger and thirst, it longs in hope of its son. If food and water are offered [in the rites] it receives them; otherwise it lets out a sigh.

18. Day after day it is marched along - two hundred and forty-seven yojans. For a full year the soul lies caught in the net of suffering.

19. Before, he never gave a thought to his deeds; the senses drove the soul along. Afterwards he fell into great affliction, and wails most bitterly.

20. Raurav with its many terrible cries, and the hell called Kumbhipak: there he undergoes the torments of hell, and no one comes to care for him.

21. He suffers hell alone, and there Yama's messengers taunt him: "You committed these sinful deeds." The ignorant one writhes in vain.

22. Bound by karma, the soul stays this way for ten million ages. It endures the buffeting of the four wombs of birth and the twenty-eight pits of hell.

23. You bound this net of karma - what offence of his was it? Day after day he says "I" and "mine", and so is noosed in birth and death.

24. In them all the "I" speaks in this way - in Brahma, in worm and in moth alike. By this word all are deceived, while you yourself remain untroubled.

25. You are unaging, deathless, stainless; karma does not touch your name. Now redeem this soul - put your hardness of heart away.

26. You are the mother and you are the father; apart from you there is no other. This soul is bearing suffering - consider this and look into it in your mind.

27. The soul is your own child; if it remembers your name, take it swiftly into your lap - your name takes it up and holds it close.

28. I entreat you, lover of your devotees, upholder of the earth, who yields himself to his devotees. You are the adamantine armour of those who take refuge; this humble one is in your shelter.

29. Only if you release us are we released; there is no other means. Otherwise Time and karma torment us - great is the blow of Yama.

30. By your name I strike down Yama and cut off the head of Time; I burn away the forest of karma and shatter the twenty-eight pits of hell.

Here ends Shri Shok Bhavan ||14||

Here begins Shri Ved Puran ||15||

1. Hari, Hari — the Vedas, the Puranas, the Smritis, the six darshans (schools of philosophy) and the nighantu (lexicon of sacred words): O Swami, I examined and looked through them all.

2. Hari, Hari — and I found one single eternal essence: the living consciousness of Hari, the Parbrahm (supreme Reality).

3. Hari, Hari — have you forgotten all the suffering of your past births? Why did you come to be again, taking lodging in the house of the womb?

4. Hari, Hari — let go of works, but do not abandon meditation on Hari; follow him day and night, in every moment and every hour.

5. Hari, Hari — swept along by your occupation, you have let the time pass away; the one task that matters is still not accomplished.

6. Hari, Hari — carried along through birth and death, through pleasure and pain: without accomplishing that task one wanders through the ages.

7. Hari, Hari — the task is not accomplished, and nothing stands to your credit; and without accomplishing it there is no home to come to.

8. Hari, Hari — that which wears a body is called the atma (soul); the one who is without a body is the Paramatma (supreme Self).

9. Hari, Hari — meditate on the Paramatma who has no image; do not busy yourself with any other elaborate show.

10. Hari, Hari — from that Paramatma everything arises, and in the end in him everything sets again.

11. Hari, Hari — one who has lost his companion weeps alone in the forest; until he sees that companion he finds no rest.

12. Hari, Hari — as a child cries at separation from its mother, and is not consoled until it reaches its mother;

13. Hari, Hari — as a fish out of water thrashes about in great distress, and has no ease until it finds water;

14. Hari, Hari — so does the soul long to abide with the Paramatma; and by that alone the task is truly accomplished.

15. Hari, Hari — Brahm alone speaks, Brahm alone listens; Brahm sees, and repeats the name of Parbrahm.

16. Hari, Hari — Vasudev, Paramatma, Parbrahm, Vishnu, Narayan: you alone are all of these.

17. Hari, Hari — O unknowing soul, why are you swept away in worldly business? In itself the soul is neither more nor less.

18. Hari, Hari — it is Parbrahm's command by which you have been kept as you are; abide within it and repeat the name of Parbrahm.

19. Hari, Hari — he is all-capable, mighty, eternal, the very essence; there is no far shore to his glory and virtue.

20. Hari, Hari — the earning of the name of Parbrahm is the true earning; without it the life-breath suffers greatly.

21. Hari, Hari — do not invent something new out of your own crooked cleverness; do not break the word of Parbrahm.

22. Hari, Hari — one who breaks that word becomes a man without a master; what refuge can there be for him now?

23. Hari, Hari — he who forsakes the Master breaks the Master's command; by any other road there is no deliverance for him.

24. Hari, Hari — this Master is true and his command is true; everything else is false and is perishing away.

25. Hari, Hari — what did not exist comes into being, and what exists is destroyed; to take the word of such things, O Swami, is hell.

26. Hari, Hari — he who is forever, who creates and who dissolves: leaving him aside, whom will you serve?

27. Hari, Hari — swept away in your business you have forgotten the Father; then who will pull you out of hell?

28. Hari, Hari — you will serve creeds and keep up religious duties, but without unwavering service it will all be ruined.

29. Hari, Hari — in many forms you have existed before this, O living soul; do you still have some craving left in you?

30. Hari, Hari — you have obtained nectar; why spill it through carelessness? There is no other savour anywhere equal to Hari.

31. Hari, Hari — why let the jewel slip out of your hand for the sake of glass? Why give up great happiness for a scrap of pleasure?

32. Hari, Hari — do not be proud, O king, lord of the earth; and do not fret and rage, O destitute pauper.

33. Hari, Hari — it is like the water of the free water-booth at Harsad: here the water is had at the price of blood.

34. Hari, Hari — by sacrifices, charity and such works a kingdom is obtained; when that merit runs out, one suffers sorrow again.

35. Hari, Hari — the happiness of the lord of the earth, the happiness of the lord of wealth, and the happiness of the tiniest creature all weigh the same.

36. Hari, Hari — whatever each one holds in his own mind to be happiness: there, O Swami, is hell complete.

37. Hari, Hari — those who have gone and taken their seat in the bliss of Parbrahm's state are not touched even by the rank of Indra.

38. Hari, Hari — abandon the mind's desires and worship Hari; the distinctions fall away and all becomes one.

39. Hari, Hari — I know no language and I know no metre; I know one thing only, O Swami: the one who ordains all.

40. Hari, Hari — by you I know and by you I live; by you, O Swami, I am released from the four wombs of birth.

41. Hari, Hari — those who are beguiled by the ashrams (stages of life), by the schools of doctrine, and by caste: without you all of them wander about lost.

42. Hari, Hari — by your command karma is mighty; yet the blind man, though it is striking him, feels no fear.

43. Hari, Hari — after enjoying the fruits of karma the soul then bears the suffering; do you feel no shame, then, for those who are your own?

44. Hari, Hari — this worthless devotee makes his plea, O Swamiji: why do you cut the soul off and keep it apart from you?

Thus ends Shri Ved Puran, complete ||15||

sections.title_en: Sorangi (a hymn in the Sorang strain)
sections.translation:
Here begins Shri Sorangi ||16||

1. Jire — I entreat Saraswat Swami and beg one favour of him: with simple, artless bhakti (devotion) I shall sing of you, who are the king of a million universes.
[refrain: Sorangia]

2. In the sorang strain let us meditate on Shri Hari; let us worship Kanhan (Krishna) of Gokul. Harji, Hari, Parbrahm who is the supreme Parbrahm — great and weighty are your names.
[refrain: Sorangia]

3. Jire — the ocean of worldly existence is hard to cross, exceedingly deep and without limit; take the name of Ram as your vessel and cross over to the far shore.
[refrain: Sorangia]

4. Jire — he who breaks and fashions a million universes: how can he be contained in a little basket? To whom shall I offer flowers and leaves, when the fourteen worlds lie inside his mouth?
[refrain: Sorangia]

5. Jire — knowing the wisdom of the Self, I delight in [unclear] his qualities. He pervades a million universes: that is the absolute Brahm, beyond all speech.

6. Jire — serve him who is tender towards his devotees; why then keep up your wailing? Serve him who removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow — hold this conviction firmly in your mind.

7. Jire — when King Ambarish was being harassed by a snare, he remembered lord Murari; and to keep the word of both the sage and the king, he took incarnation ten times over.

8. Jire — he took the form of a fish, dark of hue, and playfully churned through the ocean; in that same instant he seized the demon Panchajan in his hand and brought back the Vedas with ease.

9. Jire — Narayan took the form of the tortoise and bore Mount Mandar upon his back; gods and demons together made one company, and made the serpent their churning-rope.

10. Janardan took the form of a woman and held the pot of nectar in his hand; deceiving the demons, Hari gave it to the gods to drink, and every purpose of the gods was fulfilled.

11. Jire — in the boar form he held the earth on the tip of his tusk and set her back in her place; Hari removed the affliction of the gods, and the bones of the demons were broken.

12. Jire — in the man-lion form he tore him open with his claws and slew the demon king; bursting the pillar apart Hari came forth, and showed his grace to his devotee.

13. Jire — as Vaman he made Bali a dweller in the netherworld and removed Indra's affliction; there the Lord assumed his universal form and set his foot upon Bali's back.

14. Jire — Parashuram broke the power of the kshatriya lords and raised up the brahmin folk; he requited the wrong done to the great sage and removed his father's grief.

15. Jire — the sage's curse upon Dasharath was worked out, and all the matters were accomplished; the king performed a sacrifice and asked for sons, and there Shri Ram descended.

16. Jire — he took the incarnation of Ramchandra and did the work of the earth; for Sita's sake he slew Ravan and gave the kingdom to Vibhishan.

17. The eternal one, together with Lakshman and Sita, took the kingship of Ayodhya; the supreme Lord seated in the flower-chariot — and all the tasks were accomplished.

18. Jire — in the form of Ram he pervades everything; whatever you look upon, know it as him. See how he removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow; mighty is his command.

19. Jire — by the Vedas you are known, and yet the Vedas do not reach your far shore; pervading all in the form of Ram, you are the support of devoted folk.

20. Jire — he was born in the house of Nand the cowherd, and made Gokul his abode; to graze the cows over the twelve forests and the hill, Govind and Ram took birth.

21. Jire — earrings glitter at his ears, and on his breast a garland of gunja berries; a peacock-feather crown is set upon his head — boundless is Kanhad's beauty.

22. Jire — little Kanha the cowherd goes out to the forest to graze the cows; he eats and, eating, feeds others — he who bears up Brahma and all the gods.

23. Jire — he climbed the branch of the kadamb tree and plunged into the water of the Yamuna; Hari danced upon the hood and bridled Kali (Kaliya) the serpent.

24. Jire — his garment a yellow silk, his wrap a cloth of nine colours; Hari came riding the serpent for a saddle — that great Yadav hero.

25. Jire — in Gokul he sounded the horn, in Vrindavan he played the flute; he broke the bonds of his mother and father, and Kanha slew Kans.

26. Jire — the infinite one passed eleven years, keeping company with Ram (Balram); the teacher had him study his lessons, and he grew up in great delight.

27. Jire — for the sake of the marriage he drove Shishupal off, and wedded eight queens; and further he married women in many various ways, and had sixty lakh sons.

28. Jire — Hari came to Shonitpur and won the battle against Har-Swami (Shiv); he cut off the arms of Banasur, and Okha obtained Aniruddh.

29. Jire — Nar and Narayan came mounted on the chariot, and at that hour he showed his universal form; Hari removed the affliction of the Pandavs, destroying eighteen akshauhini armies.

30. In the Buddha form Hari pondered in meditation and took up the path of yoga; in the Kalki form, to put down the wicked, he took undying weapons in his hands.

31. Jire — let us meditate on him in all ten incarnations, and in the twenty-four of the Bhagavat; serve him who removes the anguish of the womb and every sorrow — the supreme Purush, the Lord of the world.

32. Jire — let us meditate on such a Lord of the earth, who is beyond reckoning and beyond all possibility; hard to reach even for the mind of the lord of yogis — you who are Brahma and all the rest.

33. Jire — let us sing the virtues of Govind, and meditate besides in many ways; if the Lord of compassion shows his grace, then knowledge of the Self awakens.

34. Jire — the four-armed one in the courtyard, robed in yellow silk, with the crown shining upon his head; he sports there together with Lakshmi, and the minds of the Vaishnavs are enchanted.

35. Jire — let us meditate on the imageless King, and know him both as form and as formless; follow the path of the Vedas, and bring devotion and feeling into your mind.

36. Jire — with leaves of tulsi worship the enemy of Putana; cast off delusion, envy and pride, and come to understanding through knowledge of the Self.

37. Jire — let us serve Hari together with Lakshmi, and serve his divine play and sport; he fulfils the fruit the heart desires — that King, Shri Avinash, the imperishable one.

Thus ends Sorangi, complete ||16||
The third rest of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.

sections.title_en: The Song of the Earth (the Earth's wedding)
sections.translation:
**Atha Shri Prithvi Dhol ||17|| (Vighna-haran — the removal of obstacles)**

1. Remover of obstacles, lord of all virtues, giver of the very essence of one's own understanding.
2. I sing in praise the marriage of the Earth — [of him who is] beyond the four sources of all birth.
3. I entreat the lord of Saraswati; I shall speak the word of the Niranjan (the stainless one).
4. This Earth is the maiden to be given in marriage; the bridegroom is Parbrahm, the Chakrapani (bearer of the discus).
5. The daughter has grown to full womanhood while still unwed; in all the ranks of bridegrooms there is not one who is her match.
6. Whoever is born out of pride does not endure for long.
7. In the Krita-yuga there was a king named Vena, and his pride was exceedingly great.
8. By the wrath of the sages he was struck down, and from him arose King Prithu.
9. From Prithu's name comes the name "Prithvi" (Earth); Prithu was a treasury of merit.
10. The bride is great in her virtues; among bridegrooms there is not one her equal.
11. The sage Ikshvaku, Mandhata, Sagar, Kakutstha, Dilip —
12. all of these came forward as suitors, but they died without wedding her.
13. The sage Narad went to Brahmalok and respectfully entreated the father (Brahma):
14. "Your daughter has grown to full womanhood and is still unwed — Brahma, why is your mind untroubled by it?
15. Perform the marriage without further delay; set up the sacrificial rite throughout the brahmand (the universe)."

|| Aad ||1||

**Atha Shri Saluni** (the refrain runs: "Saluni e" — O lovely one; "Sobhagya saluni e" — O fortunate, lovely one)

1. O lovely one — Brahma spoke: "Listen, O king of the brahmins." O fortunate, lovely one.
2. The maiden Earth has come to full maturity; there is no bridegroom fit for her.
3. "The greatest among gods, men and sages [am I]; the three worlds are my own creation.
4. No bridegroom greater than the Earth has been fashioned; all the rest are of baser metal.
5. There is no bridegroom greater than this daughter of mine — to whom, then, is the bride to be given?
6. Yet blame attaches to a daughter kept unwed." So then spoke the king of sages:
7. "Brahma, give heed to this request: ask the daughter herself what match she thinks fit.
8. In all the three worlds, which bridegroom pleases you? Which bridegroom in the world do you desire?
9. Tell us, child, after weighing it in your own mind." The daughter spoke: "Listen, father.
10. My bridegroom is one alone — the lord of the three worlds. In that time there was neither sun nor moon.
11. Neither demon nor man nor king was there; not one of the great sages was fit.
12. In that time there was neither wind nor the fire of the age; the waters had risen to the vault of the sky.
13. The darkness had become terrible; I had fallen into the hands of pralaya (the dissolution).
14. I was drowning there in that water; my enemy was the kalpant (the ending of the aeon).
15. I was drowning, bereft of any lord to hold me; in that moment I remembered the Swami.
16. Great is that Lord, whose form is Parbrahm, the ruler of all the worlds."

|| Aad ||2||

1. Hari, Parbrahm, you are the lord of purity; show your very great compassion upon the lowly.
2. You are the all-capable Lord, the king of Vaikunth; you laid waste the stronghold of the demons.
3. You slew the daityas and set the gods in their places; you cut away the bonds of your devotee Prahlad.
4. Hari slew the demon Narak with a stroke of the discus; all the captive princesses were set free by your grace.
5. Hari, by your grace all the wives of the gods enjoy happiness and rule, the demons driven off.
6. You released Matang (the elephant) from the torment of the crocodile; you broke down the humiliations laid on Dhruvji by his stepmother.
7. In my great distress, as I drowned in the waters — Hari, be my rescue; lift me up, Parbrahm, and come.
8. In bhakti (devotion) I praise the one Lord alone, having found the shelter of Jagannath's feet.

|| Aad ||3||

1. The merciful God, Parbrahm, became manifest; Hari, Hari, at the first he took on the form of the boar (Varah).
2. In whose ears the sky itself was held; Hari, Hari, and the light was held as it is held in the eyes.
3. The wind was held within his breath; Hari, Hari, and the surging water was held within his hoof.
4. The sky and the moon were borne on the point of his tusk; Hari, Hari, and there the Swami lifted me up.

|| Valan (the closing turn) ||

5. I was lifted up by the merciful God, the leader, the lover of devotees, in the boar form — when Brahma and Shankar were not yet, nor the creation with all its moving and unmoving beings.
6. Maker of the world, destroyer of the world, Lord of supreme bliss; Vasudev, Mukund, the great one — Krishna, Hari, Govind.

|| Aad ||4||

1. I have no other bridegroom but him alone; Hari, Hari — he who lifted me up, him alone shall I wed. This bridegroom Govind has come to dwell in my mind; Hari, Hari — for me, then, Govind alone is the whole of the matter.
2. He who freed [the maidens] from the affliction of the demons; Hari, Hari — he who wedded the sixteen thousand, him shall I wed. Brahma and the sage Narad overflowed with joy; Hari, Hari — Brahma called to mind the seven sages.

|| Valan ||

1. He summoned the seven great sages, and his mind knew boundless joy. The great sages came and fixed the lagan (the auspicious wedding hour); they examined the matching of the pair.
2. In their joy there was a clapping of hands; the chaste ones of the whole brahmand assembled. Indra, Chandra and the kings assembled; Shakti Chamunda joined them.

|| Aad ||5||

1. Yes — on the ekadashi (eleventh day) of Madhusudan, on that day was set the marriage of the Earth.
2. There every saint was sent an invitation; such were the preparations made for this wedding.
3. Mount the phuleku (the bridegroom's flower-procession); many an ovarna (the waving away of evil) was performed; the universe was decked out and hung with festoons and torans (garlanded arches).
4. There, house after house, the banners flew high; there gods and men sang dhaval (wedding songs) most beautifully.
5. There the five kinds of instruments sounded loud; gods and men gathered, and the three worlds were glad.
6. Hari's wedding party came, a delight to behold; in great joy they asked for the gift of good tidings.
7. There were flowers and tambol (betel), and the ceremony of welcome; there the apsaras danced, and there was festivity.
8. Yes — the bridegroom reached the lodging of the wedding party; the officiating priest proclaimed the bridegroom's gotra (lineage).
9. There the sages fixed and accomplished the wedding hour; the bridegroom filled the vessel brimful, and all the saints [received] the prasad (blessed offering).
10. Now send the sukhdi (wedding sweets) to the bride, for the appointed wedding hour draws near.
11. Let the bridegroom mount and set out, attended by lakhs and crores of universes.
12. Yes — at the toran (the garlanded gateway) the cries of welcome go up; let the ovarna be waved over the bridegroom Parbrahm.
13. Yes — with the call "samervate samevarte, savadhan" (the priest's summons to attention) [unclear], the madhuparka (the honey offering) is made, and many an arghya offering with it.

14. There the bride waited behind the antarpat (the cloth held between bride and groom); at the auspicious moment of the wedding the groom took the bride's hand. ||14||
|| Aad ||6||

|| Aad 7 ||
1. Ji re — of the chori (the marriage canopy), of the chori, weighty is the meaning; the chori that has been fashioned, the chori that has been fashioned, has no enclosing wall. ||1||
2. O sutradhar (master builder), O sutradhar, with full awareness raise the enclosure; make the chori out of the limbs of the four khanis (the four sources of birth). ||2||
3. A jewelled throne, and faith that is complete and unfailing; the groom and bride are seated, their hearts in great gladness. ||3||
4. Brahma is the Vaishvanar fire in which karma is offered as oblation; a hundred lakh universes are made free of karma. ||4||
5. Time itself was cooked down and made into kansar (the sweet wheat-and-ghee wedding dish); the saints serve it, the saints serve it — partake of it, O bridegroom king. ||5||
6. Remembrance is the ghee, poured over the japa (repetition of the Name); with his bride, the groom is filled and satisfied. ||6||
7. He who created the planets, the gods and the guardians of the worlds — the ten dikpals (guardians of the directions) do him service. ||7||
8. Behold him who established Dhruv; put away the bargaining and traffic of mere outward restraint. ||8||
9. The wedded couple performed the four mangals (the four auspicious rounds of the marriage rite); a hundred lakh universes were carried across. ||9||
10. The soul makes its plea to Shabda-Brahma (the Word as Brahman): O bridegroom, give heed and accept us, Hari Parbrahm. ||10||
11. O King who pervades all that is unmoving and all that moves — you have wedded us; now grant us your pasayo (grace). ||11||
12. "I am the doer, it is done by me" — thus a man is brought to ruin, and stays sunk in the trembling wombs of the four sources of birth. ||12||
13. You are for ever; you alone are. I am not — this is certain: you alone are the One. ||13||
14. With folded hands, O Lord, this much I ask: you have wedded us all — let my turning away from you be broken for good. ||14||
15. Of the anvar (the bridegroom's companion), who is Shabda-Brahma, I ask this: I am not — this is certain — before you there is the One alone. ||15||
16. The gor (officiating priest) is looked to, and the Vani (the Word) itself sings the rites; all that was given and done makes everyone glad. ||16||
17. Eighty-four lakh births — abundant is the manner of this gift; and to him is given liberation itself as the dakshina (the priest's fee). ||17||
18. Hari, Har and Brahma and the thirty-three crore gods — crores of universes all worship him. ||18||
19. Gods and men perform the ovarna (the waving rite that wards off harm); today the heart's great sorrow is broken. ||19||
20. Festival, blessing, boundless joy; through the universe rang the cry of "Jai! Jai!" ||20||
|| Aad ||7||

|| Aad 8 ||
1. Ji re — the groom and bride, having been wed, set forth; Parbrahm holds the earth in his lap. ||1||
2. Taking her with him he mounted the horse of Truth; divine is the light of Brahman. ||2||
3. Exceedingly lovely was that gathering — devotion, faith and turning-away-from-the-world were there. ||3||
4. Forgiveness, compassion and pure yearning are the singing women of the wedding party; fame, remembrance and truth attend as well. ||4||
5. The fourteen branches of learning do him service — him whom the great sages and yogis find hard to reach. ||5||
6. Moon and sun do him service; dharma ponders the supreme good (paramarth). ||6||
7. The five sounds are full of delight; drums of every kind sound and sound again. ||7||
8. Rig, Yajur and Sam sing his praise; now the bridegroom Parbrahm moves on. ||8||
9. Knowledge holds the canopy over the groom; the soul is being brought to its blessedness. ||9||
10. Contentment and dispassion wave the chamar (the ceremonial whisk); now the groom has set out for his own abode. ||10||
11. To our own mansion, the supreme state; crores of universes go along as his escort. ||11||
12. The groom passed on beyond Vaikunth, higher still; that state is cool and serene, and beyond all approach. ||12||
13. The groom reached our own mansion, the supreme state, where the King is Hari Parbrahm. ||13||
|| Aad ||8||

|| Aad 9 ||
1. That Niranjan state (the stainless, spotless state) was attained; the groom came, bringing his bride. ||1||
2. Beyond compare is that mansion — past the reach of the senses; it is both the meditation and the goal of meditation. ||2||
3. The lords of yoga, Sanak and the rest — the groom brought them all to that state. ||3||
|| Aad ||9||

|| Aad 10 ||
1. Delightful is the Niranjan state, where there is neither form nor name. ||1||
2. Where there is neither anger nor lust; where there is neither birth nor death. ||2||
3. Where there is no delusion and no falsehood; where there is neither day nor night. ||3||
4. Where there is no kind of sorrow at all; there is only light, ever-risen and unsetting. ||4||
|| Aad ||10||

|| Aad 11 ||
1. Beautiful is the Niranjan state, free of the three taps (the three afflictions), free of the sins of the six urmis (the six waves — hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, old age and death). ||1||
2. It is the unbroken dwelling place of bliss; let us worship him, the abode of Shri Lakshmi. The groom brought them all to that state. ||2||
|| Aad ||11||

|| Aad 12 ||
1. The groom, having wed, came home; welcome, Hari Parbrahm! ||1||
2. With him are Hari, Har and Brahma; with him are the gods, the sages and Indra. ||2||
3. With him are the nagas and the lords of men; with him are crores of universes. ||3||
4. Through the seven islands, the worlds and the nine regions — in happiness may all come home and abide. ||4||
|| Aad ||12||

|| Aad 13 ||
1. Great sorrows have fallen away, all are happy; happiness is found, and imagining is gone. ||1||
2. Afflictions are broken, imagining is gone; supreme bliss has welled up in full flood. ||2||
3. The Lord was beheld — Swami Achyutanand, the imperishable and blissful one; there all the saints rejoiced. ||3||
|| Aad ||13||

|| Aad 14 ||
1. Ji re — eternal Brahman, cool and serene, where there is only boundless joy. ||1||
2. Seventy-one-fold is the saints' festive joy; unceasingly let us hasten to that abode. ||2||
3. In the world of the moving and the unmoving this alone is the work to be done; I hold the Master and all else as one, and so abide. ||3||
|| Aad ||14||

|| Aad 15 ||
1. The poet entered within himself and spoke: beyond compare is Atmaram (the Self that is Ram). ||1||
2. The Master, the Master will now do the work of whoever sings the Wedding of the Earth. ||2||
3. Whoever hears the Wedding of the Earth, whoever catches the stream of Parbrahm — ||3||
4. caught, caught is the stream of Parbrahm, by the grace of Shri Padmanabh. ||4||
|| Aad ||15||

|| Here ends the Shri Prithvi Dhol, complete ||17|| ||

sections.title_en: The Great Dhol (a long devotional song)
sections.translation:
**Now begins Shri Vadu Dhol ||18||**

1. The Lord is incomparable, the one Supreme Self (Parmatma); Hari, Hari — you are the master of the soul, you are its very owner.
2. Vishnu, Govind, Narayan, Ram, Krishna — Hari, Hari — all of these are names of Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality).
3. O soul, look into your own self and break your bonds; Hari, Hari — thunder out the Name, do japa (repetition) of Parbrahm.
4. This alone is the highest good, this alone is knowledge; Hari, Hari — that meditation which is upon the name of Parbrahm.

|| Valan (refrain) ||

5. Great is the name of Parbrahm; it is the very home of righteous action.
6. Sages and siddhas rush to it in meditation; the lords of yoga gaze upon it through knowledge.
7. Vidhi (Brahma) and Shambhu (Shiva), the makers of creation — even they do not reach the far shore of his glory.

|| Valan ||

8. They do not reach the far shore of your glory, O Lord; his way cannot be found out.
9. Supreme Person, unthinkable, unmanifest — you alone are the self-existent Master.

**|| Aad ||1||**

1. Through the four wombs of birth I have wandered countless times; Hari, Hari — I never found the essence, O Lord, O Lord of liberation.
2. That light which is present in the very atom stands pervading everything; Hari, Hari — up to Hari, Har (Shiva), Brahma and all the rest.
3. Without remembering him one is never released; Hari, Hari — the soul lies bound, O Lord, in a tight, dense bond.
4. He has no form, no birth-caste, no kind or category; Hari, Hari — for him there is neither night nor day.

|| Valan ||

5. He for whom there is no day or night — worship that Light with the mantra.
6. He for whom there is no age or aeon — great beyond measure is his resolve.
7. He from whom you came into being, O soul — of him I make the refrain of my speech.

|| Valan ||

8. Of him I make the refrain of my speech: the capable and mighty Hari you have not served.
9. One who is not a devotee of the Father — know it for certain, that son has gone to ruin.

**|| Aad ||2||**

1. Sun and moon burn at his command; Hari, Hari — how shall I describe the forms he takes?
2. Earth and sky rest upon his support; Hari, Hari — how then can there be any limit to him?

|| Valan ||

3. How can there be any limit to him? Hari himself is the ten avatars.
4. Sun and moon abide by his command; how shall I tell of his forms?
5. Give up all poison, O fool — why have you forgotten the suffering of worldly existence?

|| Valan ||

6. Why have you forgotten the suffering of worldly existence? In distress, remember Govind alone.
7. He it is who establishes Brahma and Shankar; he it is who gives Indra his kingdom.

**|| Aad ||3||**

1. Crores of universes stand upon his word; Hari, Hari — how then can anything be his equal in weight?
2. His light pervades all that is unmoving and all that moves; Hari, Hari — keep your loving affection for the saints alone.

|| Valan ||

3. He sports with the saints with great affection; the all-pervading light is in every form.
4. He holds the universes by his word; there is no other who is his equal.
5. Hasten to his feet; abide in the practice of the duty of your station (varna-dharma).

|| Valan ||

6. Abide in the practice of the duty of your station; honour the one word of Vishnu.
7. Do not let sin and merit stain you in this way; you will be freed from the pain of worldly existence.

**|| Aad ||4||**

1. Shabda-Brahma (the Word as Brahman) is in love with Parbrahm; Hari, Hari — and I am intoxicated with your name.
2. Unmanifest Lord, endless, stainless; Hari, Hari — destroyer of the fear of rebirth, Shri Vasudev.

|| Valan ||

3. The devotee turns aside worldly existence and hell; that Parbrahm is the unmanifest one.
4. He who shapes the world and breaks it — no one grasps in what manner he is.
5. He in whom there is no division of any kind; whose word is the four Vedas.

|| Valan ||

6. He whose word is the four Vedas — do not abandon the original path.
7. Straying onto the wrong track of man-made doctrines — why do you fall into hell, ignorant fool?

**|| Aad ||5||**

1. He who has drunk the nectar of the unmanifest Consciousness; Hari, Hari — he has set his foot upon the head of Death.
2. Sacrifice, charity, austerity, pilgrimage, vows and mantras — Hari, Hari — all of these render their service in the name of Parbrahm.

|| Valan ||

3. All of them serve the Name; receive the fruit that it yields.
4. The fruit that is handed over is Parbrahm himself; so make yourself free of karma.
5. Let the mind run to that which is beyond the mind; thus the wall of the fear of rebirth is wiped away.

|| Valan ||

6. Thus the wall of the fear of rebirth is wiped away for one who serves with the mind's full conviction —
7. having slain the enemies: greed, delusion, lust, envy, anger and pride.

**|| Aad ||6||**

1. The unmanifest Consciousness that I had not attained; Hari, Hari — now I bind my thought upon your form.
2. Dhruv, Shuk and Narad — all of them he established; Hari, Hari — he gave them an unshakable place.

|| Valan ||

3. He gave an unshakable place to whoever repeated the Name alone.
4. Hari, Krishna, Keshav, Ram — thus many are his names.
5. He whose reign is unshakable — he has need of nothing.

|| Valan ||

6. He has need of nothing; yet the King fulfils what is in the devotee's mind.
7. To give the joy of the telling of his virtues, for that reason he takes birth in this manner.

**|| Aad ||7||**

1. The fear of karma lasted only so long; Hari, Hari — only as long as I was far away from you.
2. Prakriti (material nature) drove the soul into hell; Hari, Hari — it loaded it with crores upon crores of karma.

|| Valan ||

3. Consider the burden of a crore of deeds; they did not serve the mighty one.
4. He whose judgements are true; the shrutis and shastras have laid down their rulings.
5. Those who did not abide by that law — they were handed into the hands of Yam (death).

|| Valan ||

6. They were handed into the hands of Yam; for their deeds there are many dark hells.
7. Endlessly they suffer sorrows of every kind; the soul plays out that emptiness.

**|| Aad ||8||**

1. This ignorance has covered over the light of the eyes; Hari, Hari — blind, he forgot his home and fell into a well in the forest.
2. There the black serpent bit him; Hari, Hari — and he fell headlong into its mouth.

|| Valan ||

3. Again the dull-witted one fell into its mouth; the blind man does not see himself being destroyed.
4. O mind, let go of every other thought; take up that by which you may cross beyond worldly existence.
5. O mind, give up that scrap of pleasure; set your love upon Parbrahm.

|| Valan ||

6. Set your love upon Parbrahm day and night; O devotee, do not fail in your meditation.
7. You will attain unshakable happiness and rest; leave off the company of Prakriti.

**|| Aad ||9||**

1. Sunk in stupor by the poison of intoxication, he has lost his consciousness; Hari, Hari — how should such a one remember his home?
2. The true guru, the snake-charmer, pinned down the serpent; Hari, Hari — he awakened the blinded soul.

|| Valan ||

3. He awakened the blind one at that very moment — the one who had been in the blaze of delusion.
4. What greed there was for gathering wealth; many an agitation arose from it before.
5. Attachment to son, wife and kin; many times over there has been separation.

|| Valan ||

6. Many times over there has been separation; and still he holds the world in his mind.
7. In that which comes into being again and again and is wiped out again — what essence is there in it?

**|| Aad ||10||**

1. Sent by the Father, the snake-charmer came; Hari, Hari — with the medicine of knowledge he drew out the poison.
2. The collyrium-rod of the company of saints (satsang, holy company); Hari, Hari — that very instant the sight became clear.

|| Valan ||

3. In that instant the vision became pure; the saints' words are a rain of nectar.
4. The finest medicine is union with Parbrahm, by which the disease of worldly existence was driven out.
5. The teaching is meditation on Parbrahm; at daybreak the sun has risen.

|| Valan ||

6. At daybreak the incomparable sun has risen; the night spent in delusion is gone.
7. Letting go of [worldly] hope I found refuge; I have left the whole matter in you.

**|| Aad ||11||**

1. You are forever; I am not, not even once. Hari, Hari — this sense of "I" came to me only out of delusion.
2. Taking great pains he drew me out of the well; Hari, Hari — he showed me the road and sent me home.

|| Valan ||

[continues on the next page]

[Vadu Dhol ||18||, continued]

3. He sent home the one who had been unaware, having first made his life-breath pure.
4. The Supreme Self is the true abode; there the soul finds its rest.
5. In this way a single love-colour took hold, and the inner division was broken.

[Valan]
6. The inner division was broken in just this way: you yourself became Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality).
7. I was overtaken as the grub is overtaken by the wasp — such is the way of meditation upon You (one becomes what one contemplates).

[Aad 12]
1. Through remembrance and meditation one is absorbed in the nectar of pure consciousness; Hari, Hari — He comes as a cow comes to her calf.
2. Bound by His Name, Hari comes of His own accord; Hari, Hari — the Lord does not abandon His devotee in this perishing world.

[Valan]
3. Perishable is the companionship of worldly life; yet there the devotee has found the Lord.
4. You are Ram, the lover of devotees; true in its very meaning is Your Name.
5. The mind is set in aversion against prakriti (material nature); thus ever new are the guises You take.

[Valan]
6. Ever new are Your guises; serve the Lord Morar (Krishna) through His Name.
7. He who, knowing one to be a devotee, does not slight him — he alone, in this world.

[Aad 13]
1. Set about with ruby, pearl and gold — Hari, Hari — by sandal paste and flowers He is not pleased.
2. He who takes no delight in song, in music, in what is heard from scripture; Hari, Hari — though one dances before Him, He is not won over.
3. He who is pleased neither by cleverness nor by simplicity; Hari, Hari — how then shall we bring Him under our sway?

[Valan]
4. How shall we bring Him under our sway — He who is the father of Brahma and Shankar?
5. His own regard is this: where I myself am, there is My Name.
6. Wherever, wherever a devotee takes My Name, there, there is My abode.
7. There, there is My abode; there no one can work obstruction or terror.
8. Whoever serves Hari's Name to the very end — to him I grant a peerless dwelling.

[Aad 14]
[Tika (the commentary), Rag Godi]
1. Know Him to be such, and follow Him night and day; Hari, Hari — forsake this world, which is perishing.
2. The one imperishable is Narayan alone; Hari, Hari — He who created birth and death.
3. Those who have not been freed by this human birth; Hari, Hari — how will they be freed in any other birth?
4. Clinging to the objects of sense and driven along by household affairs; Hari, Hari — in vain is this excellent birth spent away.
5. Give up the objects of sense and turn your love to your own true good; Hari, Hari — O devotee, follow this Parbrahm.
6. Forms are only the vessels of the four wombs of creation; Hari, Hari — the primal formless One alone truly is.
7. Gods, sages, men, the unmoving and the moving; Hari, Hari — though You fashion and break them, no karma clings to You.
8. He who set sin and merit within the world; Hari, Hari — action and duty do not touch You.
9. He who created fire (Vaishvanar) with its heat; Hari, Hari — who can endure that burning of His?
10. He who brought forth the snows and the Himalaya; Hari, Hari — to what can His cooling quality be compared?
11. He who set the primal wind loose in the world; Hari, Hari — exceedingly great is that power of His.
12. He who gave knowledge to the god Maheshwar; Hari, Hari — knowledge itself does Him service.
13. All dharma and observance rest upon truth; Hari, Hari — higher still, I say, is the Name of Parbrahm.
14. The Vedas and Puranas declare it again and again; Hari, Hari — no other fruit weighs equal to the Name.
15. No end can be found to the glory and fruit of the Name; Hari, Hari — he who holds faith in it obtains that fruit.
16. Bind yourself with certainty to this one word; Hari, Hari — what austerity or rite need you then accomplish?
17. Tulsi, the Name, the tilak of gopichandan; Hari, Hari — no other fruit equals satsang (the company of saints).
18. Hold the word of scripture as certain; Hari, Hari — leave the lesser and take the greater.
19. Where the Name is absent and no thought of it ever comes; Hari, Hari — how then shall the supreme state be reached?
20. Setting aside His own mantra and inner teaching; Hari, Hari — He gave the Name to His own devotee.
21. All the rest He left entangled in disputes; Hari, Hari — those, that is, who have no faith in the Name.
22. He who has heaped up very much karma; Hari, Hari — in him faith does not arise.
23. Until karma is exhausted, faith does not arise; Hari, Hari — and lacking faith, one is born again.
24. Through crores of births, through vows, mantras and inner disciplines; Hari, Hari — it is in the last birth that faith comes.
25. Fasten the mind upon meditation on Parbrahm; Hari, Hari — even prescribed action lies in Parbrahm's hand.
26. Neither I nor anything of mine is my own; You and what is Yours alone truly are; Hari, Hari — all deeds and doings, O Lord, are in Your hand.
27. Thus lay claim to nothing and count nothing as your own; Hari, Hari — keep to good conduct and behold Narayan.
28. True and certain are You alone, O Lord; Hari, Hari — all else is perishing, false, and falling apart.
29. Whoever reads this dhol (song of praise) and reflects upon it; Hari, Hari — he is transformed and becomes Parbrahm.
30. This devotee, who is as nothing, makes his prayer, O Lord; Hari, Hari — may we obtain the refuge of the holy Guru.

Here the holy Vadu Dhol is complete ||18||

[Now begins the holy Padam Dhol ||19||]

1. Revered Guru Swamiji, I bow at your feet; Hari, Hari — I beg of you the pure understanding of the saints.
2. Pure is the city of Dwarka, the great capital; Hari, Hari — where the Lord of Vaikunth took birth.

[Valan]
3. Where the Lord of Vaikunth took birth — for the sake of the gods, with pure purpose. The Creator and Shankar, all of them assembled, to ask about dharma of Hari as Budh (the enlightened one).
4. Eagerness welled up in their bodies: "O God, what is our task?" A voice from the sky spoke out: "Turn back again today."
5. The Primal Being Himself has taken birth in Patan as a potter (Prajapat); go each of you to your own place — that is the fitting way to move.
6. Brahma, Shankar, Indra and the gods, the thirty-three, men and women alike; when Hari took birth in the world of mortals, they became human beings in the world.
7. He was born on the bank of the Sharada, and swiftly they gathered this time. In Patan he is called Padam, and is known as a potter (kumbhkar).
8. His father is the doer and cause of all, Lakhma is his mother, Patal De his chief queen — I will go and bow at Hari's feet.
9. With folded hands I make my prayer and swiftly bow my head; I will go and tell my errand there, where the Lord of the age has taken birth.
10. Some took birth in the manner of Janak, some in the form of Shuk and Narad; some remained detached, and some became mighty kings.

[Valan]
11. Some became mighty kings, O Lord; Your true form cannot be told. Each one found his own place by the grace of Shri Padmanabh.

[Aad 1]
1. Lord and servant met, and the secret was made plain; Hari, Hari — very great was the joy in our hearts.
2. O God, be gracious with your feet and tell us: Hari, Hari — for what purpose this strange, contrary incarnation?

[Valan]
3. "In strange ways I have taken birth many times before. I delivered Shankh and recovered the beloved Vedas — that was the Fish (Matsya) incarnation.
4. In the Tortoise (Kurma) form I churned the ocean and took out the fourteen jewels; on my back I bore Mount Mandar and stirred the sea, and the purpose of gods and men was fulfilled.
5. I held the earth on the tip of my tusk, taking the Boar (Varaha) form; out of love for the world I preserved the kings upon the earth.
6. Taking birth in the Man-Lion (Narsinh) form, I slew Hiranaksh; I established Prahlad and gave him his station, with all the immortals as witness.
7. In the Dwarf (Vaman) form I became a brahmin and begged of King Bali; I pressed him down to Patal, the serpent trembled, and he asked a boon of grace.
8. Taking birth as Parshuram I set upon crores of Kshatriyas; I gave the earth to the brahmins and stood there with folded hands.
9. In the form of Ram I slew Ravan and won Sita back [unclear]; in that earlier, seventh incarnation you were the monkeys and the bears.
10. In the eighth I took birth, and you as the Yadav clan; I was Krishna the cowherd and you were mine — and swiftly Kans was conquered.

[Valan]
11. Swiftly Kans was conquered, O Lord, and we went to Dwaramati; I settled a city twelve yojan wide on the pure bank of the Gomti.

[Aad 2]
1. In the ninth I took birth to keep my given word; Hari, Hari — to do away with the cause of karma.
2. The sages do not know this secret of mine; Hari, Hari — the Vedas and Puranas make their entreaty.

[Valan]
3. The Vedas and Puranas make their entreaty; no one knows the secret. Hari took birth in the form of Budh, to uphold dharma for the age.
4. To do away with the karma of the world, and to dissolve the seed of the gunas (the qualities that bind); to carry beings across the world — such was the plea made to the Lord of the age.
5. Twelve devotees will appear, and the universe will resound; Vishnu spoke in the form of a Vaishnav, to set free every region of the world.
6. He turned fools into the virtuous and made the wicked into saints; He showed mercy upon us, the lowly, and forgave many an offence.
7. Many a time He has ferried souls across when demons blocked the road; Shri Padmanabh came, and made a landing-place for liberation.
8. Wood and body were made spotless, and the waters were made pure; in this way the fallen were uplifted, and thereafter became the bodies of saints.
9. He granted pardon to the six schools of philosophy and contentment to all alike; through satsang everything was obtained, and the old disease of birth departed.
10. All have fallen into the ocean of worldly existence; sinking, they find no farther shore. As in Janak's way, uplift the whole age this time.

[Valan]
11. Uplift them this time, O Lord, in love for the world; Shri Padmanabh took incarnation and redeemed all four wombs of creation.

[Aad 3]
1. Dwarka and Kashi are crest-jewels among strongholds; Hari, Hari — how shall I tell the fame of the Vadi (the sacred garden)?
2. From the stainless (niranjan) state Parbrahm took birth; Hari, Hari — in Patan, as a potter, Shri Padmanabh.

[Valan]
3. Shri Padmanabh took birth in due union, and the earth's purpose was accomplished. To us paupers a jewel has come to hand; today eagerness wells up in our bodies.
4. As wealth comes to a man who has none, so the enemy's work was broken; He gave liberation to the eighty-four lakh species and did great good to others.
5. The Vadi is Vaikunth's own seat made manifest, where the light of Brahm shines; men and women sing there of Parbrahm's state and dwell in the stainless state.
6. All the saints were called near, and the earth's work was accomplished: tilak, tulsi and satsang — take Hari's Name upon your lips.
7. Taking birth upon the earth, He was worshipped as the very essence of purity; moving with the majestic gait of an elephant, He set the world free.
8. All the saints sat in bliss, and divine knowledge arose among them; the King of Vaikunth sat in their midst and gave the highest gift.
9. All the world's sorrow was shattered and boundless gladness arose; the drums of the gods sounded, and cries of victory filled the universe.
10. Celestial chariots moved toward Vaikunth, and Yam's road was broken; in city after city festoons and banners were raised, and there was a great throng of the gods.

[Valan]
11. There is a great throng of the gods, O Lord, by the grace of Shri Padmanabh; by Padmanabh's grace the perils of Yam (death) have been removed.

Here the holy Padam Dhol is complete ||19||
The fourth vishram (resting-section) of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.

sections.title_en: The Ras (round-dance song) of the Garden
sections.translation:
Here begins the holy Vadi no Ras (the Ras of the Garden) ||20||

-- Ad 1 --

1. First, within the city of Dwarka -- Hari, Hari -- Hari took birth, moving by a course contrary to all expectation.

2. Before this you were Matsya (the Fish), Kurma (the Tortoise), Varaha (the Boar) -- Hari, Hari -- Narsinh (the Man-Lion), Vaman (the Dwarf), Parshuram.

3. You are Ram, you are Krishna, compassionate and Niranjan (the stainless one) -- Hari, Hari -- of endless forms, and beautiful.

4. In the ninth turn Hari took birth in the form of Buddh (the Buddha) -- Hari, Hari -- he held meditation and set the japa (repetition of the Name) going.

|| Valan (the turn of the refrain) ||

5. He held meditation and set the japa going, and the cry of victory went up through the world. Shri Padmanabh came there, to set the universe right.

6. He moves among the saints like the full moon. As the orb of the sun shines in the sky, so shines this new moon.

7. Dark-hued and lovely, lord of the cows, Gopal. Hari establishes dharma and cuts karma away; he appears full of mercy.

8. As a rain-cloud rises up, so he rains down bhakti (devotion). At the night-vigil the deep sound resounds there; the sages and gods throng about him [unclear].

9. The tilak (forehead mark), the tulsi (sacred basil) and the Name are the weapons by which Shrinath redeems. Listen -- he speaks the nectar-word: he has placed these in the hands of the Vaishnavs.

10. Bali, Vibhishan, Ambarish, Narad, Dhruv and Prahlad -- and to his friend Sudama he gave refuge; to Ajamil he gave his call.

11. He made his form manifest -- the unknowable one cannot be reckoned. Leaving Vaikunth he came into the vadi (garden) at Patan.

12. That garden is a lovely grove; it looks like Kailas. It is Brahma's abode, the stainless state, where the hopes of devotees are fulfilled.

|| End of Ad 1 ||

-- Ad 2 --

1. Countless devotees perform your service -- Hari, Hari -- the thirty-three crore gods together with Indra.

2. The Creator, Shankar, the gods and the sages come asking -- Hari, Hari -- they fall at your feet, O Lord.

3. Lord of the three worlds, the stainless one -- Hari, Hari -- crusher of the demons, the merciful Lord.

4. Exceedingly tender, unfathomable, without division -- Hari, Hari -- beyond the Vedas, he stands pervading all.

|| Valan ||

5. He stands pervading all, having established the universe, and he kept his Name hidden. He summoned Shambhu (Shiva) and Brahma and entrusted the work to them both.

6. "Lover of his devotees" is your title; you alone are the great king. Mighty is your lila (divine play) -- and thus you have set it going.

7. Earth, sky, mountains, and the waters of the seven seas -- in a single instant they would break their bounds; they hold only by your word.

8. Even to those who abuse him he does good -- such a mighty king is he. Even those who came in enmity were redeemed; the demons were swept from their place.

9. Turning his love upon others -- whoever fell within his gaze -- he ended their dwelling in the womb and ferried those people across.

10. Over the whole earth and the fourteen worlds, what you do is what happens. Look for your equal: there is no second, no other is to be seen.

11. Crusher of pride are you, O Lord, protector of the universe. "I do it, it comes about through me" -- all that is empty talk.

12. What you do comes to pass -- speak this as the true word. Everything else perishes; let the mind hold no division about it.

|| End of Ad 2 ||

-- Ad 3 --

1. There is no division for the one by whose remembrance [we are saved] -- Hari, Hari -- serve him always, every single day.

2. Hari is the supreme life, the treasury of all virtues -- Hari, Hari -- a crore of holy places do him service.

3. Bringing unfailing, single-pointed faith into the mind -- Hari, Hari -- O living beings, make your japa of Parbrahm.

4. What he speaks comes about; what is not, does not come to be -- Hari, Hari -- by his darshan (sight of the divine) all become four-armed.

|| Valan ||

5. By your darshan, Lord, all become four-armed gods. The four wombs of birth are redeemed, and it costs you not a moment's trouble.

6. Driven by lust, anger and greed, a man has no clear sense of a single thing. Maya has him chained in chains -- how then is he to remember you, O Father?

7. The mountains of craving are exceedingly many, and within them are cruel blows. They can be crossed over only if you, Hari, take care of us.

8. The bondage of karma has arisen; with what means do I come to birth? I go about within egotism, in the company of prakriti (material nature).

9. The ocean of worldly existence is hard to cross; there is no daily ferry over it. Within it delusion shows itself like a crocodile; without you there is no farther shore.

10. One is led astray in the illusion of pilgrimage; one practises yoga; one is dyed in the colours of women; one longs for enjoyments.

11. I have found your Name to be the very essence; faith has come into my mind. Joy has surged up in my body; you dwell in my heart.

12. Countless were redeemed before this -- crores who walked the path of great karma. Those who were joined to the Name of Parbrahm broke the bonds of worldly existence.

|| End of Ad 3 ||

-- Ad 4 --

1. By whose remembrance one is released from calamity -- Hari, Hari -- one is released, O Lord, from hell and from dwelling in the womb.

2. One attains the unmoving abode of the stainless one -- Hari, Hari -- experience that changeless rest.

3. There is bliss forever where the supreme bliss is -- Hari, Hari -- there joy and delight are exceedingly great.

4. There is no darkness there; there is light alone -- Hari, Hari -- the saints sport with Hari forever.

|| Valan ||

5. The saints sport with Hari forever, and the Name is the one thing that counts. What you do comes to pass, O Father of the three worlds.

6. Taking birth in the form of the Fish, he swiftly brought back the Vedas. To Shankh he granted refuge and removed the division of worldly existence.

7. In the form of the Tortoise he churned [the ocean] and took the fourteen jewels. Many demons were crushed, and there the purposes of gods and men were accomplished.

8. In the Boar's form the cause of the universe held the earth upon his tusk. Swiftly he stopped her from sinking -- blessed, blessed is the boar's tusk.

9. In the Man-Lion's form he tore Hiranyakashipu into a crore of pieces. He established Prahlad, cut his bonds, and gave him an unshakable kingdom.

10. In the Dwarf's form he became a brahmin and begged a gift of Bali: "Give me three paces of earth, a place for me to stay."

11. Parshuram took up the axe and finished the work of the kshatriyas. He gave the earth away to the brahmins, and then Shri Ram took birth.

12. You yourself are Ram, you yourself are Krishna; there is no end to your prowess. Kans and Ravan were delivered -- it did not take an instant's delay.

13. In the Buddha's form he held meditation -- the first supreme bliss. Singing the virtues of Parbrahm, bliss arises in the mind.

14. To wipe away the stain of the Kali age, the Lord is Nishkalank (the one without stain). The Vaishnav says: at the tenth turn he will take birth this time.

|| End of Ad 4 ||

Here the holy Vadi no Ras is complete ||20||

Here begins the holy Laghu Ras (the Short Ras) ||21||

1. Thus was Shri Padmanabh, the Parbrahm, met -- and seven lakh crore were set free. Freed were the creatures and living beings from having to be born again. O Narhar! -- they were freed.

2. The four wombs of birth were made pure -- it is your grace, O Father. Every one of them goes forth having become liberated. O Narhar! -- every one.

3. Indra and the other gods rejoiced, and the thirty-three crore sages. In the twenty-one universes the kettle-drums sounded. O Narhar! -- the universes.

4. Brahma and the rest, and Shiv, were delighted: "We have attained Parbrahm." What they attained was the Creator, master of endless universes. O Narhar! -- the Creator.

5. The eight families of mountains became four-armed, and so did the nine families of serpents. The eighty-eight thousand were released from the penances they had to perform. O Narhar! -- they were released.

6. Hari the sun rose, and then the night of delusion passed away. In his rays the thousand names of Parbrahm shone forth. O Narhar! -- in his rays.

7. Listen, all you Vaishnav people: this is the word of King Parbrahmji. What I speak is not a matter of mere comparison. O Narhar! -- it is not.

Here the holy Laghu Ras is complete ||21||

sections.title_en: The Ras of 'Chatur Vadan' (with a skilful tongue)
sections.translation:
Here begins the Ras of Chatur Vadan ||22||

1. With a skilful tongue remember Him who was there at the beginning of the age, by whose grace Shiva slew Tripur. With sound I praise the Lord's virtues. Hari, Hari.

2. Hari's word (vani) pervades every world; remember it in the mind, turning your thought to the good path. Know Him to be the highest deity. Hari, Hari.

3. Day and night remember the one stainless One, the breaker of old age, death, sorrow and the fear of rebirth, the delight of the sages: hold Him in your thought. Hari, Hari.

4. Brahma and the rest never reach the end of His qualities; utter the name of Govind even once. The Lord is the almighty king. Hari, Hari.

5. The fallen Ajamil called out to his son (who bore the name Narayan); by that name Narayan he was carried across worldly existence, and he came to rest in the supreme state. Hari, Hari.

6. His stepmother put him down from her lap; by the name of Narayan Dhruv reached his goal, and he stayed there, taking the unmoving station. Hari, Hari.

7. Whatever comes of sacrifice, charity, austerity and pilgrimage, the fruit of Hari is far greater than all of it: meditate on Him by night and by day. Hari, Hari.

8. The fruits of many meritorious deeds are loudly proclaimed, yet all of them are put to shame before the repetition of Hari's name; by it the round of births is broken. Hari, Hari.

9. By Hari's name whole families of sins are destroyed; the lord of Samyamani (Yama) and his servants take fright, and they never again set their hope on such a one. Hari, Hari.

10. As the sun's rays sweep away the darkness, so no karma stands before the repetition of Hari's name; in Kaliyug this is proof before your own eyes. Hari, Hari.

11. Treat the senses as enemies and disregard them; see Narayan in all that moves and all that does not move; count every being as equal to yourself. Hari, Hari.

12. Whoever has grasped the greatness of the Name has made his unshakeable dwelling in the supreme state; he has drunk of supreme bliss. Hari, Hari.

13. King Ambarish worshipped Hari; with full faith he fulfilled the observance of Hari's day, and thereby he obtained His grace. Hari, Hari.

14. Ambarish was spared any further dwelling in the womb; the Lord went forth to take the curse upon Himself, and the sage's trick and stratagem was defeated. Hari, Hari.

15. Though the birth was from a low-born servant woman, Hari was pleased with him; by the power of the Name, Narad was perfected and at once received the fruit of liberation. Hari, Hari.

16. Consider that in time everything perishes; twist down and kill desire, anger and pride; the essence of it all is to repeat Hari's name. Hari, Hari.

17. Shankar knows the savour of devotion to Vishnu; he brings his mind to meditation on Ram's name. Do not let that thought go for even a moment. Hari, Hari.

18. Let a man perform the duty of his station with right discernment and do good deeds; serve with feeling and follow Narayan; in the end he attains the state of Hari. Hari, Hari.

19. According to one's karma an understanding arises; according to that understanding action is done; and so a life is spent. Hari, Hari.

20. The net of karma is torn by Hari's name; by remembrance day and night the bonds fall away; in this way dwelling in the womb comes to an end. Hari, Hari.

21. Janak Vipashchit, by devotion alone, looked with skill upon the souls in hell; that saint brought them to liberation. Hari, Hari.

22. What the King's decree lays down is fitting; and again the King's decree may seem unfitting; make it fitting by Your name. Hari, Hari.

23. Prahlad kept Him within his heart; he showed Narhari manifest to his father; that testimony stands to the end of the aeon. Hari, Hari.

24. The soul, without awareness, has given itself over to the power of karma; the King's decree stands, pervading the world; He has established the qualities of nature, which break apart in a moment. Hari, Hari.

25. Shuk, Sanak and the rest pursue their own doctrine; they turn over yam and niyam and the rest in their hearts; still they do not reach His farther shore. Hari, Hari.

26. Reasoning by false doctrine, they set up a wrong path; they abandon the King's decree that the Veda upholds; they [unclear] the world of Yama. Hari, Hari.

27. They prescribe forgiveness, compassion and contentment, yet they blot out the King's decree that the Veda upholds; they plant a wrong-minded thinking. Hari, Hari.

28. With the many arguments of this or that scripture they fall into hell and lose the human birth; they do not reach the farther shore. Hari, Hari.

29. The word of the unmanifest Parbrahm: know it, in accord with the Veda, to be unshakeable; His command is the mighty one. Hari, Hari.

30. Each of the several schools praises its own; in Kaliyug they do not know the true form of Vishnu; they come to birth in the four wombs of existence. Hari, Hari.

31. Hari Narayan alone is the lord of liberation; without Him even one devoted to yoga does not obtain it; day after day keep up the practice. Hari, Hari.

32. Those whose birth and death have been broken sit at rest; leaving the objects of sense they have entered the supreme aim; at the end they beheld Murari. Hari, Hari.

33. The supreme Person, the unmanifest Madhusudan, uprooter of countless fears of rebirth and of sins: Ram, the destroyer of the wicked. Hari, Hari.

34. Keep in mind Him who speaks the truth; throw away everything else as false; hold to this one thought. Hari, Hari.

35. Keep Hari in the mind and bind yourself to Him with certainty; accomplish union with Parbrahm, the state of liberation; practise your own dharma. Hari, Hari.

36. The King is unshakeable and His word is unshakeable; stay unwavering, bringing faith into the mind; by repeating the Name a man finds his place. Hari, Hari.

37. Those who have taken delight in this ras and given themselves to it, their fear of dwelling in the womb is broken, by the grace of Hari Parbrahm. Hari, Hari.

Thus ends Shri Chatur Vadan (the Ras), complete ||22||

Here begins the Ras of Aharnish ||23||

1. I bow to the One, undivided and indivisible, whose form the Vedas cannot grasp; unaging, deathless, stainless, without form, who created the eighty-four lakh kinds of forms. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

2. Do not spend yourself on anything else, you proud fool. He who brought forth many universes out of His mind, by that very name you cross over existence. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

3. In countless lives you have taken birth; you have borne hardship and much sorrow; and now, in the pride of wealth, you have forgotten Him, and there are yet countless thousands more to come. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

4. Nothing touches Him, nothing clings to Him or defiles Him; in a moment He breaks and fashions ten million universes; He deceives them all, the clever and the simple alike; standing apart, He stages many a play. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

5. He who dwells beyond ten million universes, who but a Vaishnav can grasp Him? His way is one without precedent; remember Him, for through His leela (divine play) Hari gives liberation.

6. Listen, soul, I tell you one secret: do not, in your ignorance, say "I" and "mine". Get yourself across by the name of Parbrahm; in this way your Father will call you home.

7. In the beginning and before the beginning You alone are; all that stands still and all that moves is Your radiance. You are great, and so are Your names; with all the saints, my salutation is to You.

8. There is no likeness for the nectar of Hari's virtues; even knowledge of the spirit is no match for it. Gods and yogis perish at the end of the aeon, but the saints, contented in Hari's virtues, remain unbroken.

9. Many things in the world seem good, but without Hari's virtues they are all a blaze of poison. Where Hari's virtues are loved day and night, there the fear of death has fled.

10. What you see is certainly perishing; why then cling to any of it with longing? Mighty maya has made you blind; the Guru's word is the true collyrium for the eyes.

11. At first the mouth tastes sweetness, and then the fish falls into great agony. Just so the deluded soul is swept along by pleasure; know that death has taken hold, and fate will do its work.

12. The senses are the servants and the mind is the chief minister; driven by them, a man abandons knowledge. Draw your own self away from them, so as to reach the state of Parbrahm and cling there.

13. Gold weighed out, cows and land given away, food and water given with great honour: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

14. They read the Vedas and Puranas to the very end, they performed sacrifices, vows and observances: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.
