15. They practised austerity and discipline for a long time and gave up the household and the snare of maya: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

16. One accomplishes the yoga of the spirit and gives up comfort and the enjoyment of the finest savours: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

17. They practise truth and purity daily and worship the gods together with meditation: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

18. They serve mother, father and the Guru's feet, and practise forgiveness, compassion and vows: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

19. Vows, pilgrimage, fasting and ritual works, hospitality to guests and strangers, the dharma of compassion to living beings: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

20. They give up slander and abuse of others, though they praise themselves in false disputation: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

21. They cast off desire, anger and envy, and give pain to no one: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

22. They hold back and restrain all the senses; they endure fasting, harsh austerity and cold: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

23. The four wombs of birth bring only turmoil and hunger; the earning of dharma brings strong happiness. By the name of Parbrahm hunger is broken; the unmoving state was obtained and every distress removed.

24. Renouncing the world he came to the Guru's shelter, and conquered birth, old age, fear and death. Devotees, follow the Guru's shelter; the savour of the Guru's word holds him every day.

25. Night and day the savour of His qualities has become his very feeling; he has let go of all other moods, good and bad. In the company of the saints joy wells up and overflows. Parbrahm says: how then should any ruin come to him?

26. Dhruv, the sun and the moon abide in the remembrance of Hari; before that they had borne the afflictions of worldly life. Yakshas, kinnars and men became free of poison; Narad set free beings of the three worlds.

27. The sage named Puru and the husband of Rambha: by remembrance they made an end of worldly existence. If your business is to be lord of the earth, then serve king Parbrahm with bhakti (devotion).

28. Consider and look at the body and the universe: no one can set up an equal to Him. Himself without form, He spreads out this whole expanse; He is from the beginning the father of Brahma and Shankar.

29. By the Name Ajamil attained his end; by the Name the courtesan's birth was carried through. Such is the Name and so powerful; why then cling in vain to what brings ruin?

30. Parbrahm, heed this one petition: the deluded soul strays about in the world. Make it pure and take it into Yourself; make it one with You, and grant it happiness.

31. Lord, heed this one petition: this world is Your own utterance. Your own portions repeat Your name; for the whole world, moving and unmoving, this alone is the work.

32. Whoever sings this ras with a single mind, whoever hears this ras with a single mind, is released from the noose of worldly bondage, which is hard to win even for Brahma and Maheshwar. Grant that grace, Lord Parbrahm. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

Thus ends Shri Aharnish (the Ras), complete ||23||

Here begins the holy Sant Sohago ||24||

1. The virtues of Govind are utterly beyond compare; we shall sing the Sant Sohago, the saints' wedding-song.

2. Singing those virtues one attains great bliss; the Lord's name is Niranjan, the Stainless One.

3. In the beginning the Earth was a maiden, unwed. "Tell us, O goddess, which bridegroom pleases you?"

4. Proudly she answers: "King Niranjan, and no other -- no man can stand equal to the weight of the earth."

5. It was for this reason that the maiden had remained unwed: to look upon the King of Dwarka.

6. Made pure by the thousand names, she seeks the bridegroom of this house: "Lord of the world, why do you remain unwed?"

7. "Summon Brahma, who recites the four Vedas; let him declare the secret of this match between bride and bridegroom."

8. "He has no mother, no father, no brother, no kinsfolk of his own -- and to the wicked he shows no mercy.

9. "Such an almighty bridegroom as Niranjan is the one we want; but how is that Purush, that Supreme Person, to be known?

10. "How can the wedding day be fixed for one of whom no one has any notion -- at whose house even Yam, the lord of death, waits upon him as a servant?"

11. The bridegroom is welcomed with the wedding procession and the whole universe is redeemed; now Vaikunth-city itself has come down into the mortal world.

12. The bridegroom mounted his steed; the Perfect Purush was found. The Lord of endless universes, Parbrahm himself, has come.

13. At the wedding-arch the bridegroom took his bride, and old age and death were undone; this thing was accomplished for all creation, moving and unmoving.

14. Bridegroom and bride, the two of them, are now brought together; the merciful Lord is the giver of every happiness.

15. Hand was laid in hand and the maiden's ceremony was fulfilled; Hari of his own accord was satisfied, brimming with joy.

|| Aah ||1|| (the second song follows, numbered afresh)

1. O, tie the wedding canopy of the heart -- for the Lord has shown exceedingly great mercy.

2. O, summon the officiating priest after due thought, and hold the Lord of Vaikunth in your heart.

3. O, bridegroom and bride have both come, and the priest had the endless universes set free.

4. O, the two of them are seated, brimming with joy; they have crossed the ocean of worldly existence and reached the far shore.

5. O, through Vasudev's union Hari came into the world; by the name of Hari all sins have been wiped away.

6. O, let the dhaval-mangal, the auspicious wedding songs, be sung, knowing the Earth to be the bride; before this, into the [unclear] pavilion, Sita was brought.

7. O, let such auspicious rites be performed with a knowing mind; there every creature and living being receives the gift of liberation.

8. O, set out the wedding square, knowing him to be the four-armed one; and utter your every word with Govind-Ram.

9. O, prepare the kansar, the wedding sweet, and leave off ritual works; set out the offering-platter with the thousand names.

10. O, take the ceremonial sip of water, bringing your mind to his feet; and utter your every word with Govind-Ram.

11. O, honour the betel-leaf with true conviction of mind; Hari has redeemed those who stood by their given word.

12. O, the thirty-three gods have gathered in a crowd to watch; upon Parbrahmji has come [unclear: soli -- apparently the full bridegroom's array].

13. O, Sanak and the other sages look on and rejoice: now this bride has become the equal of the bridegroom.

14. O, Indra, Ishvar and Brahma recite the Vedas there; yet the nirgun Narayan, the Lord without attributes, takes no delight in any of it.

15. O, the Protector of his people took her hand in marriage; and all merit and all sin he carried away to Vaikunth.

16. O, in the age of Kali, Krishna in his endless forms, in his very form as Parbrahm, wedded the Earth.

17. O, know the two of them to be equal, both of them Hari; therefore do bhakti (devotion) to Parbrahm.

18. O, the endless universes cry out "Victory, victory!"; in the name of Parbrahm all rejoice.

Here the holy Sant Sohago is complete ||24||

sections.title_en: The Song of Grace (a plea for the Lord's favour)
sections.translation:
Here begins the holy Pasavalo ||25||

1. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from self-interest -- turn it away from self-interest; Hari, Hari, grant us in great abundance the highest good that lies in your Name.

2. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from falsehood and crooked understanding -- turn it away from falsehood and crooked understanding; Hari, Hari, grant us right understanding, O Master of the three worlds.

3. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from "I" and from pride -- turn it away from "I" and from pride; Hari, Hari, you who are Niranjan, the stainless Master, come and dwell in our heart.

4. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from the taste of the senses -- turn it away from the taste of the senses; Hari, Hari, let me repeat your name unbroken, O Master.

5. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from fancies about others -- turn it away from fancies about others; Hari, Hari, give us instead, in great abundance, the thought of your Name.

6. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from another man's wife -- turn it away from another man's wife; Hari, Hari, let me delight in your Name before all else.

7. Turn our mind away, O Lord, from sleep, that enemy -- turn it away from sleep, that enemy; Hari, Hari, let it not break the repeating of your name.

8. Grant our mind, O Lord, bhakti (devotion) and loving feeling -- grant it bhakti and loving feeling; Hari, Hari, it is to you, Parbrahm, that I make my plea.

9. Grant our mind, O Lord, the company of the saints -- grant it the company of the saints; Hari, Hari, so that through you, Parbrahm, my [unclear: vigat -- my separateness, or my wretched condition] may be wiped away.

10. Grant our mind, O Lord, detachment and faith -- grant it detachment and faith; Hari, Hari, fulfil the hope that is in my heart.

11. Thus prays the Vaishnav, the servant of Harji -- thus prays the Vaishnav, the servant of Harji: Hari, Hari, I ask only for a dwelling place at the feet of the saints.

Here the holy Pasavalo is complete ||25||

sections.title_en: The Ubhavalo -- a traditional song-form (the printed heading reads Ubhavalo; exact sense of the name is unclear)
sections.translation:
Here begins the holy Ubhavalo ||26||

1. Lovely, lovely is he -- the King of Vaikunth has been found! Fair is the bridegroom of Rukmini; he has wiped out sins from their very seat. Take the name of Narayan. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm. My Govind-Ram, I take refuge at your feet.

2. I read and read, and mastered all four Vedas; I lost myself on the path of ritual works and went wandering. I never came to know the secret of bhakti (devotion). Caught up in many things, I bow my head. Repeat the name...

3. O gods, O gods -- the God of gods has been found, the Master of all Vaikunth! Serve him, serve him -- he who tore Hiranyakashipu apart. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

4. He wore, he wore the yellow silken robe, and put on a garland of gunja berries. This cowherd lad took up the bamboo flute, and work and household were all forgotten. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

5. Enchanted, enchanted were the thirty-three crore gods; enchanted were the cowherd women of Gokul. This cowherd lad, this herdsman boy, has put an end to the dwelling in the womb -- he has lifted us out of the mother's lap of rebirth. Repeat the name...

6. Lakshmi, Lakshmi -- the husband of Lakshmi has been found, Damodar, the grinder of poverty to dust. Filled with joy, filled with joy are your saints, when your glance falls upon them. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

Here the holy Ubhavalo is complete ||26||

Heading: Now begins the Shri Khandana (the grain-pounding song) ||27||

1. I know nothing of singing or of playing instruments; Hari, Hari - with a single, undivided mind I simply praise the fair Ramji.

2. As I sang of Govind an eager longing took hold of me; Hari, Hari - and the wandering delusion of ten million births was broken.

3. When you sing of Govind, do not hold back out of shyness or regard for what others say; Hari, Hari - for by that singing the dwelling in the womb, birth after birth, will be destroyed.

4. O blind one, why have you forgotten the house of the womb and its suffering? Hari, Hari - you are tied fast in the noose of maya (worldly illusion).

5. Take up the sword of Hari and cut that bond; Hari, Hari - then you will not fall into the grip of this world again.

6. The clatter of coming and going, of birth and death, is broken; Hari, Hari - at his feet I have found Govind and hold him fast.

7. Ramji, Ramji, Ramji, O Ram; Hari, Hari - it is your Name, O Lord, that I wait upon and serve.

8. Wherever I look, there I see Ramji; Hari, Hari - how then could I turn away from him, my beloved Ramkrishna?

9. Wherever I look, there is your radiance; Hari, Hari - show me your affection, O Master of the three worlds.

10. The name of Ram is what carries the three worlds across; Hari, Hari - it wards off hell, O Lord Vasudev.

11. Whoever lives in any manner at all without bhakti (devotion) to Vishnu; Hari, Hari - is like a man with a lamp in his hand who, being blind, still falls into the well.

12. One who utters "Vishnuji, Krishnaji" day and night; Hari, Hari - how could such a one go on being spread out and scattered through the three worlds?

13. Feed on Brahman, worship Parabrahma; Hari, Hari - by Brahman the whole universe has been upheld and delivered.

14. He who fashioned universes so vast as these; Hari, Hari - he set the moon and the sun in them as lamps.

15. If the longing is there, then Vasudev arises within; Hari, Hari - and a Vaishnav (devotee of Vishnu) is made in the company of the saints.

16. May the company of saints be mine, and in great abundance; Hari, Hari - for in that company the fair Ram is found.

17. The guru gave me the sweet of Ram's Name; Hari, Hari - and the hunger of ten million births was broken.

18. Ramji, Ramji, Ramji, O fair one; Hari, Hari - with you the one soul is [unclear: "fudo", apparently "false" or "deceitful"].

19. One man goes to the Ganga and to Gaya and comes back; Hari, Hari - but he who remembers Ramji gains a greater fruit than that.

20. With every single syllable of the Name there is a bathing in the Ganga; Hari, Hari - and he who remembers that holy word attains the supreme state.

Closing: Here the Shri Khandana is complete ||27||

Heading: Now begins the Shri Hindola (the swing song) ||28||

Refrain, repeated through the song: "O swing! - yoga, the union with God, is the essence of the whole inner spiritual path."

1. Let us meditate on Hari the formless; let us worship that Parabrahma. Let us long for the stainless state, O swing - the state where there is neither birth nor death. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

2. O swing - the Vedas cannot reach the far shore of his glory. O swing - day and night, meditation on Parabrahma. O swing - that is the resting place of the soul. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

3. Let us give up the pleasures that perish, and the many rich enjoyments of heaven too. Let us serve instead the happiness that never breaks off, O swing - the union of the devotee with Parabrahma. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

4. The sorrow of ten million births is cast away, and supreme bliss has arisen. Let us sway in the happiness of the liberated state, O swing - for the primal Mukund has been met and embraced. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

5. Gods and great sages have served him, yet the Lord does not grant them his darshan (sight of himself). The Vaishnavs reach him effortlessly, O swing - there, where "I" and "mine" do not exist. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

6. By sacrifices, by charity, by vows and by austerities my births were not brought to an end. You are all-powerful - now let me serve you, O swing - now, now let there be deliverance from the womb. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

7. The bonds of karma have been cut through, and the four sources of birth [unclear: "sanjheri"]. The path of death has been shut off, O swing - Parabrahma is the very life-breath of his devotee. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

8. Knowledge and dispassion were made the festive arch, and Shankar and Brahma its two pillars. Desireless bhakti is the little swing, O swing - and on it Hari Parabrahma sways and sways. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

9. At the first push of the swing he shaped the world; at the second he sustains the universe; at the third he gathers the three worlds back into himself, O swing - and at the fourth there is no creation left at all. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

10. The poet makes his prayer with the word that is Brahman: O King Parabrahma, give heed. There is none who knows more than you, O swing - now carry this soul across. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

11. O swing - the Vedas cannot reach the far shore of his glory. O swing - day and night, meditation on Parabrahma. O swing - that is the resting place of the soul. O swing - yoga is the essence of the spiritual path.

Closing: Here the Hindola is complete ||28||

Colophon: The fifth vishram (resting-section) of the five-day parayan (recitation) is complete.

|| Ath Shri Arjun Gita ||29||
Dhanraj-Adhyaruji Maharaj rachit

Shri guru pratape gaiye | kirpa te sadhu jan ||
Parbrahm maro atma | marun man te Arjun ||
Arjun suno gita sar | Pandav manjo nidhari ||tek||

Tyare Arjune em ja puchhyun | tamo sambhalo Vaikunthray ||
Ek sar gita kaho swami | nij bhaktno mahimay || Arjun ||1||

Tyare Shri Hari valtun ocharya | tamo Arjun dharjo man ||
Ek sar gita sambhale | avatar teno dhanya || Arjun ||2||

Chaud lok vash mahare | vali brahmand kero bhar ||
Te dhanya dhanya mara dasne | mane rakhe rude mojhar || Arjun ||3||

Jal madhye jem padma chhe | tene sparsh nahi re lagar ||
E chinh mara dasnun | jene valge na vishay vikar || Arjun ||4||

Sansarman sarso rahe | ne man mari pas ||
Mayaman lubdhe nahi | te jan maro das || Arjun ||5||

Muj bhakt te mujne bhaje | jene haiye het hamesh ||
To bhakt tene janiye | je kare na koino dvesh || Arjun ||6||

Ek mane mujne bhaje | antar ani [unclear] ||
Bhakt tyare janiye | jivno te thay shiv || Arjun ||7||

Karman tulsi karne tulsi | kanthe tulsi har ||
Bahu tilak chhaya shobhatan | muj bhaktno shangar || Arjun ||8||

Mara bhaktne jane nahi | pakhand puje lok ||
Bahu dambh adambar kare | te janun sarve phok || Arjun ||9||

Uttam thai mune na bhaje | chandal kahie teh ||

Mara bhaktne jane nahi | chandal kahie teh ||
Te mara bhakt kere karane | musal nikandu eh || Arjun ||11||

Hun Ishwar chhun jad jivno | mare nahi maran avatar ||
Chhatan bhakt kere karane | hun deh dharun chhun sar || Arjun ||12||

Muj bhakt kere karane | avatar lidha dash ||
Hun Niranjan Nirakar | te mane bhakte kidho vash || Arjun ||13||

Vali bhakt kere karane | hun gayo vasme van ||
Men Ravan mari rajya apyun | Vibhishan rajan || Arjun ||14||

Durvasa rushie dubhavyo | muj atma Ambarish ||
Bhay chakra meli chhediyo | men bhali lagadi shikh || Arjun ||15||

Balirayne men bandhiyo | devoni kidhi sar ||
Patal apyun rayne | tyan hun rahyo chhadidar || Arjun ||16||

Gokul vishe hun avataryo | sir pichh dharto mor ||
Khato hun makhan taskari | jugman kahevayo chor || Arjun ||17||

Vali Jashodae mane bandhiyo | hun jodi rahyo behu hath ||
Din thayo mara dasno | hun chaud bhuvanno nath || Arjun ||18||

Vali Indra jyare kopiyo | tyare koie na avyun ad ||
Men Gokul rakhyun reltun | Gopine ladavyan lad || Arjun ||19||

Vali solsen sahasman hun ramyo | maro koie na jane bhed ||
Mara bhakt kere karane | mune kahe lampat ved || Arjun ||20||

Viranchi vachharun hari gayo | te kari gayo ja adharm ||
Hun navan nipjavi laviyo | maro koie na jane marm || Arjun ||21||

Tahan Kanse mujne marvane | mokalya daitya apar ||
Men tehne sanharine | Vrajni kidhi sar || Arjun ||22||

Mamane hun malva gayo | tyan mali Kubja nar ||
Thodak chandan karane | men apyun rup apar || Arjun ||23||

Vali pratham pole pesatan | pariyate didhi gal ||
Men marine vastar lidha | sohaviya goval || Arjun ||24||

Vali tyanthi agal chaltan | malan lavi har ||
Men arth sadhyo ehno | apya padarath char || Arjun ||25||

Vali margman napik malyo | men apyun darpan hath ||
Purna manorath te tana | men rakhyo mari sath || Arjun ||26||

Sambandhi te janne hane | chandalno te ansh ||
Mara bhakt kere karane | men maryo mamo Kans || Arjun ||27||

Men Sudamane santoshiyo | ek kangna kanne kaj ||
Sampat api tehne | nav nidh sidh ath || Arjun ||28||

Ek var Vidur gher jai | arogya bhaji pan ||
Men lad padyan mara dasna | rayna modyan man || Arjun ||29||

Pachhi Kaurav kul sanghariyun | men saryo taro arth ||
Hun chaud bhuvanno rajiyo | men hankyo taro rath || Arjun ||30||

Ek var to hun vanman gayo | tahan van disatan ghanghor ||
Men bhav joyo bhiladino | juthan te prasyan bor || Arjun ||31||

Ame ghanan mali govaliya | ramta te gaya maha van ||
Bahu bhav joi rushi narno | ame jachi te lidhan ann || Arjun ||32||

Prahlad pitae parabhavyo | men khambh mahi puryo vas ||
Dusht daitya vidariyo | men rude rakhyo das ||33||

Vali Dhruvne dukh pamadyo | ne kadhyo vanvas ||
Te balake mane vash karyo | dhan dhan maro das || Arjun ||34||

Chandrahasne Harishchandra raja | bhakt mara teh ||
Pade vipat na visare | muj mugatna mani eh || Arjun ||35||

Jyare Sudhanvane lai nakhiyo | tate tel balti jhal ||
Mara dasne vela padi | tyare turat kari sambhal || Arjun ||36||

Draupadi kera patful kadhyan | hun pas nahi te kal ||
Mara bhaktne vela padi | turat kari sambhal || Arjun ||37||

Panchaline jyare parabhavi | pase te huta panch vir ||
Mara bhaktne men puriyan | navsen nevanun chir || Arjun ||38||

Ek kolie kautak karyun | ane lidhun marun rup ||
Rayni kanya parabhavi | par dal kopya bhup || Arjun ||39||

Men tyan jaine shun karyun | marun tej mukyun may ||
Pardalno parajay karyo | marun birad padyun tyay || Arjun ||40||

Ajamil maha pataki | mamki gunika jeh ||
Je smaran kartan maharun | Vaikunth pohoti teh || Arjun ||41||

Gajrajne grahe grahyo | tyan lidhun marun nam ||
Em ek kartan behunan | men kidhan tehnan kam || Arjun ||42||

Hun man ne mara bhaktman | antar na hoy lagar ||
Muj bhaktne olakhe nahi | te bhuli bhame sansar || Arjun ||43||

Mahara bhakt dukhiye hun dukhi | sukhiye te sukhiyo jan ||
Mahara bhaktne jo dubhave | te mane mare ban || Arjun ||44||

Swarg mrutyu patalman | jal thal maharo vas ||
Tatva kahun hun tujne | hun thaki adko das || Arjun ||45||

Jap yagno nahi malun | nahi tap tirath ke dan ||
Arjun mahima janjo | marun bhaktithi chhe gyan || Arjun ||46||

Hun bhaktni sange pharun | mane bhaktno adhar ||
Arjun mahima janjo | kaheta na ave par || Arjun ||47||

Hari bhakt mahima suni | Arjun pamya harakh apar ||
Murchhit thai avani padyo | netre vahe jaldhar || Arjun ||48||

A gitane je anubhave | je gay nar ne nar ||
Arjun evun janjo | te pame pad nirdhar || Arjun ||49||

E bhakt mahima maharo | kone kalyo nav jay ||
Jenun bhagya hoy te anubhave | Dhandas gita gay || Arjun ||50||

|| Iti Shri Arjun (Dhandas) gita sampurna ||29||
sections.translation:
|| Here begins the Shri Arjun Gita ||29|| - composed by Dhanraj-Adhyaruji Maharaj

Opening refrain (tek): By the grace of Shri Guru let us sing, by the mercy of the sadhu-folk. Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality) is my very soul; my mind is Arjun. Arjun, listen to the essence of the Gita; O Pandav, hold it as certain.

1. Then Arjun asked this: "Listen, O Lord of Vaikunth. Tell me, master, the one essential Gita - the greatness of your own devotee."
2. Then Shri Hari answered: "Arjun, set your mind upon this. Whoever listens to this one essential Gita - blessed is his birth."
3. The fourteen worlds are under my sway, and the burden of the whole universe is mine as well; yet blessed, blessed is that servant of mine who keeps me within his heart.
4. As the lotus stands in the midst of water and the water does not touch it in the least - that is the mark of my servant: no craving or corruption clings to him.
5. He lives fully in the world, yet his mind stays close to me; he is not caught by greed for maya (illusion) - know him to be my servant.
6. He is my devotee who worships me with love always in his heart; know that one to be a devotee who bears hatred toward no one.
7. He who worships me with a single mind, holding [unclear] within - know him then to be a devotee: his jiv (individual soul) becomes Shiv.
8. Tulsi in the hand, tulsi at the ear, a tulsi garland at the throat, many tilak marks shining upon him - that is my devotee's ornament.
9. Those who do not recognise my devotee, and worship shams instead; who make a great show of hypocrisy and pomp - all of that I count as empty.
10. He who, though highborn, does not worship me - call him an outcaste; he who, though an outcaste, worships me - know him to be my own body.
11. He who does not recognise my devotee - call him an outcaste; for my devotee's sake I uproot such a one, wiping out his very family line.
12. I am the Lord of every inert creature; for me there is neither death nor birth - yet for my devotee's sake I truly take on a body.
13. For my devotee's sake I took the ten avatars (incarnations); I am Niranjan, the stainless Formless One, yet the devotee has brought me under his sway.
14. Again, for my devotee's sake I went into the harsh forest; I killed Ravan and gave away the kingdom, making Vibhishan king.
15. When the sage Durvasa wronged Ambarish, who is my own soul, I loosed the dreaded chakra (discus) and cut him down - I taught him a good lesson.
16. I bound King Bali and looked after the gods; I gave the netherworld to that king, and there I myself stayed on as his doorkeeper.
17. I was born in Gokul, wearing a peacock feather on my head; I ate butter by stealth, and in the world I was called a thief.
18. Jashoda too bound me, and I stood there with both hands joined - I, the lord of the fourteen worlds, became humble before my own servant.
19. Again, when Indra raged, no one came forward to stand in the way; I kept Gokul from being washed away, and fondly indulged the gopis.
20. Again, I sported among the sixteen thousand (solsen sahas) - no one knows my secret; for my devotee's sake the Veda calls me a libertine.
21. Virinchi (Brahma) carried off the calves - in doing so he did an unrighteous thing; I made new ones and brought them back, and no one knows my mystery.
22. There Kans sent countless demons to kill me; I destroyed them and took care of Vraj.
23. I went to meet my maternal uncle, and there the hunchbacked woman Kubja met me; for a little sandal-paste I gave her boundless beauty.
24. Again, as I entered the first gate, the washerman abused me; I struck him down and took the clothes, and adorned the cowherds with them.
25. Going on further from there, the flower-woman brought a garland; I fulfilled her purpose and gave her the four padarath (the four great gains of life).
26. Again, on the road a barber met me; I placed a mirror in his hand; his longing being fulfilled, I kept him with me.
27. One who kills his own kinsman is a portion of an outcaste; yet for my devotee's sake I killed my uncle Kans.
28. I satisfied Sudama for the sake of a single grain of parched millet; I gave him wealth - the nine treasures and the eight siddhis (powers).
29. Once I went to Vidur's house and ate the leaves of a plain pot-herb; I indulged my servant fondly and broke the pride of kings.
30. Then the Kaurav clan was destroyed and I accomplished your purpose; I who am king of the fourteen worlds drove your chariot.
31. Once I went into the forest, and there the woods looked dark and dense; I saw the Bhil woman's devotion, and ate the berries she had already tasted.
32. Many of us cowherds together went playing into the great forest; seeing the deep devotion of the sages' wives, we begged and took food from them.
33. When Prahlad was tormented by his father, I filled the pillar with my presence; I tore the wicked demon apart, and kept my servant in my heart.
34. Again, when Dhruv was given pain and driven out into the forest, that child brought me under his power - blessed, blessed is my servant.
35. Chandrahas and King Harishchandra - they are devotees of mine; when calamity falls they do not forget me: these are the jewels of my crown.
36. When Sudhanva was picked up and thrown by his father into oil blazing in flames, my servant's hour of trial came, and at once I took care of him.
37. When Draupadi's garment was pulled away, I was not near her at that moment; my devotee's hour of trial came, and at once I took care of her.
38. When Panchali was dishonoured, her five heroes were standing right beside her; for my devotee I supplied nine hundred and ninety-nine lengths of cloth.
39. A Koli man played a trick and took on my form; he dishonoured the king's daughter, and the enemy host and its king were enraged.
40. What did I do when I went there? I placed my own splendour within him; I defeated the enemy host, and established my good name there.
41. Ajamil was a great sinner, and so was that courtesan [unclear: "mamki"]; merely by remembering my name, she reached Vaikunth.
42. When the crocodile seized the king of elephants, there he uttered my name; thus by doing one deed I accomplished the purpose of both of them.
43. Between me and my devotee there is not the least distance; whoever does not recognise my devotee wanders lost through the world.
44. When my devotee grieves I grieve; when he is happy, know that I am happy; whoever wounds my devotee shoots an arrow into me.
45. In heaven, on earth and in the netherworld, in the waters and on the land is my dwelling; I tell you the truth of it: my servant is greater than I am.
46. I am not to be reached by muttered prayer or sacrifices, nor by austerity, pilgrimage or charity; Arjun, know this greatness: knowledge of me comes through bhakti (devotion).
47. I move about in the company of my devotee; the devotee is my support; Arjun, know this greatness - it cannot be told to the end.
48. Hearing the greatness of Hari's devotees, Arjun was filled with boundless joy; he fainted and fell to the ground, streams of water flowing from his eyes.
49. Whoever experiences this Gita, whatever man or woman sings it - Arjun, know this: he surely attains that state.
50. This greatness of my devotee is my own, and no one can fathom it; he whose fortune it is, experiences it - Dhandas sings this Gita.

|| Here ends the Shri Arjun (Dhandas) Gita, complete ||29||

Putra bhave jene lidhun nam | mukti sarkhun apyun tham ||bolo ||4||

Gunka sarkhi te mugti gai | teni sakh brahmande gai ||
Janma ja chhuti bhav santap | juo Hari nam tano pratap ||bolo ||5||

Dait rup Hiranyakashipu nam | tene Harisu karyo sangram ||
Ochhange lai odharyo veri | ap sarikho karyo Hari ||bolo ||6||

Ravane kehvi bhakti ja kari | Ramchandrani gharuni hari ||
Judh kartan lidhun nam | te jan pamyo Vaikunth dham ||bolo ||7||

Krishna tana dveshi bhupal | Jarasangh Shalva Shishupal ||
Kans Kalayavan mad mod | odhariya apradhi krod ||bolo ||8||

Ambarish anudin poshe pran | tene Krishnane melyun ban ||
Veman betho sur pekhtan | odhariyo Arjun dekhtan ||bolo ||9||

Dhruv Amarish Prahlad vakhan | avichal pad pamya nirvan ||
Bal Vibhishan Narad Shesh | moto mahima namno joy ||bolo ||10||

Vaishnavjan thai dharvun dhyan | sakal santne karo pranam ||
Hari vina jene kidhan dharm | teto jano saghla karm ||bolo ||11||

Kund athavis narke bharya | Vaishnav janke thala karya ||
Sant tanun tyan lagyun vay | chhutya nam tene mahimay ||bolo ||12||

Jap tap tirath jag ja karya | sakal dharam tene acharya ||
Kidhan vrat didhan bahu dan | jene mukh ek Parbrahm nam ||bolo ||13||

Char vedno sar e dhar | Vishnu tanun je nam uchar ||
Sakal shastranun tatva e jan | e nishche hainde man an ||bolo ||14||

Te nar dahya mota jan | jehne dhyan ek Sarangpan ||
Sarav gyan je bhaniye jeh | Ram tano ras mane jeh ||bolo ||15||

Dhan dhan kahiye te nar nar | jehni vani vase Murar ||
Hari kirtan gaye sambhale | te nishche Parbrahmne jai male ||bolo ||16||

Harijan maha mohochhav karo | Hari sabad harakhe ocharo ||
Nam tano jehne adhar | mahare Vaishnavjan parivar ||bolo ||17||

Vishnu vina je dhariye dhyan | te jano saghlun agyan ||
Vishnu vina je bijun dharam | te jano saghlun adharam ||bolo ||18||

Janam kot bhage abhas | te Hari nam teno prakash ||
Niranjan pad pame vas | jehvo Thakor tehvo das ||bolo ||19||

Sant sangat mali Hari gun gav | Parbrahmni vani mukh ocharo ||
Harinun bhajan kari lyo lahav | Vaishnav janno e mahimay ||bolo ||20||

Sant renuka mastak dharo | Parbrahmjinun chintvan karo ||
Nam tano avyo vishvas | Nath bhane Vaishnavno das ||bolo ||21||

|| Iti Shri Nam Pratapni Parchari sampurna ||30||

Iti Shri Adhyarujinan kirtan sampurna
sections.translation:
|| Here begins the Shri Nam Pratapni Parchari - the account of the power of the Name ||30||

Refrain (dhru): The king of a crore of universes rejoiced, and he performed one great act of grace: Ram, the knower of every heart, was pleased, and he grants a place to the Vaishnav (devotee of Vishnu). Say it, saints: Hari Parbrahm, victory to Parbrahm! Swami Padmanabhji, we are in your refuge.

1. Know that Shri Padmanabhji has come down as an avatar to redeem all four kinds of birth; he took care of the world and freely released liberation out of his own treasury.
2. The tilak mark, the tulsi, Hari's name in the mouth, and the company of the saints - this is true rest; the four padarath (four great gains of life) are obtained if we bow our head to the Vaishnav.
3. The greatness of Hari's name has no limit; Brahma and the other gods turn it over in their minds; searching and searching they found the essence: the Name alone releases one from the round of worldly existence.
4. Look at Ajamil, that great sinner - there was no other like him; he uttered the Name meaning only his son, and was given a place equal to liberation.
5. Even such a courtesan went to liberation, and the testimony of it spread through the universe; birth itself was ended, and the torment of worldly existence - see the power of Hari's name.
6. There was a demon named Hiranyakashipu who made war upon Hari; taking that enemy upon his lap Hari redeemed him and made him like himself.
7. What kind of bhakti (devotion) did Ravan practise! He carried off Ramchandra's wife; yet, uttering the Name while he fought, that man attained the abode of Vaikunth.
8. The kings who hated Krishna - Jarasangh, Shalva, Shishupal, Kans, Kalayavan whose pride was broken - crores of such offenders were redeemed.
9. Ambarish nourished his life day after day; he loosed an arrow at Krishna; seated in a celestial chariot while the gods looked on, he was redeemed before Arjun's very eyes.
10. Dhruv, Amarish and Prahlad are praised; they attained the unshakable state and nirvan (final release); Bali, Vibhishan, Narad and Shesh - see how great is the glory of the Name.
11. Become a Vaishnav and hold that in meditation; make obeisance to all the saints; whatever religious duties are done without Hari - know them all to be mere karma (empty action).
12. The twenty-eight cauldrons were filled with hell; the Vaishnavs emptied them out; the breath of the saints touched that place, and by the greatness of the Name they were set free.
13. He has done japa, austerity, pilgrimage and sacrifice, and has practised every religious duty; he has kept the fasts and given much in charity - he who has the one name of Parbrahm on his lips.
14. Hold this to be the essence of the four Vedas: to utter the name of Vishnu; know this to be the truth of all the scriptures - fix this with certainty in heart and mind.
15. Know those men to be wise and great whose meditation is on Sarangpan (Vishnu, bearer of the bow) alone; whatever knowledge we may study - it belongs to the one who tastes the savour of Ram.
16. Blessed, blessed we call that man or woman in whose speech Murari (Krishna) dwells; whoever sings and listens to Hari's kirtan (hymn) will surely go and meet Parbrahm.
17. O people of Hari, hold a great festival; utter Hari's word with joy; those whose support is the Name - the Vaishnav folk - are my own family.
18. Any meditation held on anything other than Vishnu - know it all to be ignorance; any religion other than Vishnu - know it all to be irreligion.
19. The illusion of a crore of births is broken - such is the light of Hari's name; one comes to dwell in the state of Niranjan (the stainless Lord): as the Master is, so is the servant.
20. Meeting in the company of the saints, sing Hari's praises; utter the word of Parbrahm with your mouth; take the profit of it by worshipping Hari - this is the glory of the Vaishnav.
21. Place the dust of the saints' feet upon your head; contemplate Parbrahmji; faith in the Name has come - so says Nath, the servant of the Vaishnavs.

|| Here ends the Shri Nam Pratapni Parchari, complete ||30||

Here end the kirtans of Shri Adhyaruji, complete.

|| Arti ||1||

Arti Sadguru Jivanjiki | sakal sant mali karo kirti ||
Nam nav chadhi par utare | anek jivke karaj sare ||
Nam rupko sabko dradhayo | sab sante mali Hari gun gayo ||
Sant samagam aharnish kije | Ram rasayan anudin pije ||
Das Dayal sadguruke sharana | jathe mit jaye avagavana ||

|| Arti ||2||

Arti Ramkabirki kije | Hari Hari anant kot jahan sant biraje ||
Prem prakash sakal bharpura | yah Saheb santanmen nura ||
Sab santanke puran kama | Trehta manhe padhare Rama ||
Dusht vidaran sant odharan | Krishna nam hai jivke taran ||
Sundar sukh par karat nochhovari | mata Jashodae arti utari ||
Sab gopi mali ras banave | Krishna-Kabir Jivan ave ||
Lila kare Vrindavan manhe | Das Dayal charanki chhanhe ||

|| Arti ||3||

Jay Gurjar disha | Prabhu jay Gurjar disha ||
Puniyad mukame padharya (2) Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj ||jay||
Am bhaktona taran kaje | avya Gurjar desh | Prabhu avya ||
Vrindavanna vasi (2) avya sadguru thaine aj ||jay||
Gopaldasne guru banavi | banya bhaktona das | Prabhu banya ||
Ramkabirnun nam (2) apyun am bhaktone aj ||jay||
Ramkabirni punya naukaman | amne besadya aj | Prabhu amne ||
Krupa sadgurujiki (2) utare bhav par ||jay||
Bal Gopalni mukti kaje | apyo ek updesh | Prabhu apyo ||
Ram Krishnanun samran karjo (2) kaljugman adhar ||jay||
Jivanjini arti | sarva bhakto mali gaye sarve bhakto ||
Das Jivan jyan pragatya (2) bhakto sevak thai ave ||jay||
sections.translation:
Arti 1 (the lamp-offering)

1. This is the arti of Sadguru Jivanji; let all the saints gather and sing his praise.
2. Boarding the boat of the Name, he carries one across; he accomplishes the purpose of countless souls.
3. He made the Name and the Form firm in everyone; all the saints together sang Hari's praises.
4. Keep the company of the saints night and day; drink the elixir of Ram every single day.
5. Das Dayal is in the refuge of the Sadguru, by which coming and going (rebirth) is ended.

Arti 2

1. Perform the arti of Ramkabir - Hari, Hari! - there where endless crores of saints are seated.
2. The light of love fills all things; this Saheb (Master) is the radiance within the saints.
3. He fulfils the desires of all the saints; Ram came down in the Treta age.
4. Destroyer of the wicked, redeemer of the saints - the name of Krishna is the deliverance of the soul.
5. Beautiful joy is waved over him and offered up; mother Jashoda performed his arti.
6. All the gopis gather and make the ras dance; Krishna-Kabir Jivan comes.
7. He plays his lila (divine play) in Vrindavan; Das Dayal rests in the shade of his feet.

Arti 3

1. Victory to the land of Gujarat - Lord, victory to the land of Gujarat!
2. He came to the place Puniyad (twice) - Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj. (Victory!)
3. To carry us devotees across, he came to the land of Gujarat - Lord, he came.
4. He who dwells in Vrindavan (twice) has come today, become our Sadguru. (Victory!)
5. Making Gopaldas a guru, he became the servant of the devotees - Lord, he became.
6. The name of Ramkabir (twice) he gave to us devotees today. (Victory!)
7. In the holy boat of Ramkabir he seated us today - Lord, he seated us.
8. The grace of the Sadguru (twice) carries us over the ocean of existence. (Victory!)
9. For the liberation of the young cowherd folk he gave one teaching - Lord, he gave it.
10. Remember Ram and Krishna (twice) - that is the support in the Kaliyug (the dark age). (Victory!)
11. This is the arti of Jivanji; let all the devotees gather and sing it, all the devotees.
12. Where Das Jivan appeared (twice), devotees come and become his servants. (Victory!)

|| Ath Sharanu ||

Jivanji Maharaj magu sharanu tamaru | Sharanu tamaru rama sharanu tamaru ||
Krishnadasne bhakti api | Sarve bhaktoni kashti kapi ||1||
Bhoja Gujarno uddhar kidho | Keshavdasne sharane lidho ||
Guru sandhate yatra vishe | Marwadne ugaryo ||2||
Krishna Keshavne nimit karine | Kantho Surat taryo ||
Padmanabh Gnaniji dada | Shukdevji Gopal ||3||
Jivanji e krupa karine | Ugarya sahu bal ||
Ramkabirni dradh naukama | Jivanji besade ||4||
Krupa karine Kabir krupalo | Bhavsagar utare ||
Jivanjina bal gopalo | Ramkabir ucharo ||5||
Bhavsagarthi taravano e | Sundar chhe bahu aro ||
Ananya bhakti nam nishtha ne | Satsangatine dharo ||6||
Avivas ne dushit bhojan | Salil sangne taro ||
Nihshank hoi ne bhajan karo to | Nam phale tatkal ||7||
Muj papine sharane lidho | Eva din dayal ||
Sadguru Jivan chho nijnam | Jivan Krishna Jivan Ram ||8||
Sadguru Jivan chho nijnam | Jivan Kabir Jivan Ram ||
Harmaba par krupa karine | Kanam Pal ugari ||9||

|| Iti Sharanu sampurna ||

Prasad upar tulsi patra mukti vakhate bolvani
sections.translation:
|| Here begins the Sharanu (the prayer of taking refuge) ||

Opening line. Jivanji Maharaj, I beg for your refuge — your refuge, O Rama, your refuge.

1. You gave Krishnadas the gift of bhakti (devotion); you cut away the sufferings of all the devotees.

2. You brought about the deliverance of Bhoja Gujar, and took Keshavdas into your refuge. On pilgrimage in the company of the Guru, you saved Marwad.

3. Making Krishna and Keshav your instruments, you delivered the coastal country and Surat. Padmanabh, the wise elder Gnaniji, Shukdevji, Gopal —

4. Jivanji showed his grace and rescued all these children of his. Jivanji seats them in the steady boat of Ramkabir.

5. Showing his grace, the compassionate Kabir carries them across the ocean of worldly existence. O children and cowherd-boys of Jivanji, utter the name "Ramkabir".

6. This is a beautiful and ample landing-place for crossing over the ocean of existence: hold fast to undivided bhakti (devotion), steadfastness in the Name, and satsang (holy company).

7. Cast away faithlessness, defiled food, and [unclear: "salil sang" — literally "watery/loose company", apparently bad company]. Worship without any doubt, and the Name bears fruit at once.

8. He took even me, a sinner, into his refuge — such is he, merciful to the lowly. Sadguru (true master) Jivan, you are the very Name itself: Jivan is Krishna, Jivan is Ram.

9. Sadguru Jivan, you are the very Name itself: Jivan is Kabir, Jivan is Ram. Showing his grace upon Harmaba, he saved the Kanam and Pal regions.

|| Here the Sharanu is complete ||

sections.title_en: Couplets for the Prasad (sanctified food offering)
sections.translit:
|| Sakhi ||

Vege Vrunda tere piyakun bulao | Bhav prat kar bhojan pao ||
Shakpak jhajhanke hoi | Bhav prit Hari lijo soi ||1||
Ashta patrani lijo bulai | Arti karat Jashoda mai ||
Sol sahas su bhojan kije | Juthan Jivandaskun dije ||2||

|| Sakhi ||
Sab sakha brijnarsu | Aroge Jadupatiray ||
Juthan pave Jivana | Sadguru tane pasay ||1||

Prasadni Sakhi
Ram kahe sukh upaje Krishna kahe duhkh jay ||
Mahima maha prasadko pavo prit lagai ||1||
Prasad lai pavan thaya ane purya manna kod ||
Dhan dhan Nagar Narsaiyane jene gher padharya Ranchhod ||
sections.translation:
|| Sakhi (couplet) ||

1. Quickly, O Vrinda (the tulsi plant), call your beloved; with true feeling and love, let him take this food. Though the vegetables and cooked dishes be many, O Hari, accept that which is offered with feeling and love.

2. Call the eight chief queens too; mother Jashoda performs the arti (waving of lamps). Let the sixteen thousand take their meal, and give what is left over to Jivandas.

|| Sakhi (couplet) ||

1. Together with all the companions and the men of Braj, Jadupati Ray (Krishna, lord of the Yadavas) partakes of the food. Jivana receives the leavings of that meal, by the grace of the Sadguru (true master).

[Heading on page 176:] Couplets for the prasad.

1. Say "Ram" and happiness arises; say "Krishna" and sorrow departs. Great is the glory of the maha-prasad (the great sanctified food) — partake of it with love.

2. Taking the prasad they were made pure, and the longings of their hearts were fulfilled. Blessed, blessed is Narsaiyo the Nagar, at whose house Ranchhod (Krishna) came in person.

sections.title_en: Couplets for Tying the Kanthi (sacred neck-thread)
sections.translit:
Kanthi bandhva mateni sakhi

Kanthi bandi chhodki lije sharan tumhar ||
Das nimit kachhu bhayo tum jano Kirtar ||1||
Kanthi tilak dharke graho Ramkabir adhar ||
Das garibi grahi raho utaro bhavjal par ||2||
Yah bano Radha Krishnako guru krupate deu ||
Dhirajse dhare raho krupa kare Gurudev ||3||
|| Ramkabir ||
sections.translation:
Couplets for the tying of the kanthi (the sacred neck-thread of initiation).

1. With the tying of the kanthi, loosen my bonds and take me into your refuge. The servant is only an instrument; whatever has come to pass, you know it, O Creator.

2. Wearing the kanthi and the tilak (forehead mark), take Ramkabir as your support. Servant, hold to humility and you will cross to the far shore of the ocean of worldly existence.

3. This garb belongs to Radha and Krishna; I give it to you by the grace of the Guru. Keep wearing it with patience, and Gurudev (the divine master) will show his grace.

|| Ramkabir ||
